screening_results.reason: Although this paper reports whole-brain fMRI in healthy humans performing a perceptual decision-making task with appropriate within-task contrasts (and reports group-level, voxelwise activation maps), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study investigates metacognitive confidence in a face/house perceptual task rather than cue-reactivity to reward/drug-related visual cues, so it is not relevant to the review topic. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. This study used a noninstrumental outcome-prediction task with deterministic monetary gains/losses and applied multivoxel pattern (searchlight) fMRI analyses. It does include group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps derived from searchlight decoding and reports results in figures and coordinates (satisfies I6 and I7). However, it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (no risky>safe, ambiguity, or hard>easy contrasts); the task is outcome prediction without risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty, and no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because ALL required inclusion criteria are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports an fMRI probabilistic category learning (weather prediction) task (feedback-based learning), not reward-cue reactivity. Against the inclusion criteria: it does not clearly meet I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined for this review), does not meet I5 (no contrasts explicitly defined as risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts), and does not meet I6 (group-level analyses were constrained by an a priori mask rather than an unmasked whole-brain task-evoked map). The paper does report voxel coordinates and task-related activations in tables/figures (I7 met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore excluded for failing to meet required inclusion criteria and not addressing the review objective.

This is an fMRI study where human participants performed a risky decision-making task (CUPS gambling task) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted. The paper reports within-task contrasts (risky vs non-risky trials, main effects of decision and feedback) and parametric modulation analyses (risk and reward), with group-level whole-brain results (FLAME, thresholded maps) presented in figures and tables. Thus it meets I4 (risky decision-making fMRI task), I5 (task contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Recommendation: INCLUDE for meta-analysis of fMRI studies of reward-related cue-reactivity in the context of task-evoked whole-brain activation.

Although this study meets the methodological inclusion criteria for decision-making fMRI studies (see below), it does not address the stated meta-analysis objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. This paper reports an active risky decision-making task (BART) with monetary rewards and investigates parametric modulation by pump number, recent outcomes, and striatal D2/D3 binding—rather than passive visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural-reward cues. Therefore it is not conceptually aligned with the meta-analysis objective and is excluded.

Although this paper reports whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI of a risky decision-making (framing) task and provides voxelwise contrasts and coordinates, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study examines genetic modulation of amygdala/ACC responses during a framing decision task (no drug or natural reward cues, and no cue-reactivity paradigm with visual reward stimuli). Therefore, despite meeting technical fMRI inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7), it is not relevant to the review question and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of probabilistic reversal learning in adolescents and adults, so it meets I4 (task-based risky/uncertain decision-making) and I5 (within-task contrasts: PFB vs NFB-Stay/NFB-Switch etc.). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses (ACC, VS, vmPFC) and does not provide a clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or coordinates/results from whole-brain statistics. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Additionally, the study does not address the review’s focus on drug/natural reward cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. This is an fMRI study of tactile perceptual decision making (tactile pattern discrimination; saccadic responses) and does not involve reward-related or visual cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task parametric modulation/contrast related to perceptual difficulty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM and activation maps), I7 (results reported in text/figures/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it does not address the review’s topic (no reward cue-reactivity, no visual reward cues).

This is an fMRI study in human participants using the risky-gains decision-making task (risk task), with explicit within-task contrasts (risky vs safe) and between-group comparisons. The analysis is whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level (linear mixed effects, voxel-wise thresholds and cluster correction reported), and results are reported as whole-brain clusters/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4–I7 are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that implemented a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination with graded difficulty and noise trials) (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., parametric modulation by signal strength, FaceDecision > HouseDecision, hard/medium/easy manipulations, and related GLM contrasts) (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain z-thresholding, cluster correction, and reported activation maps including nucleus accumbens and vmPFC), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6). Results and contrasts are described in the main text and figures/tables (acceptable reporting formats) (I7). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study reports fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task (an ambiguous/risky decision-making task), includes within-task contrasts for decision/outcome phases (advantageous vs. disadvantageous choices; wins vs. losses), and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses in addition to ROI analyses. Whole-brain between- and within-group results are described (posterior cingulate/precuneus, MPFC, etc.), meeting the requirement that whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/results are available in the text/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective: it uses olfactory (odor) stimuli, not visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards, and the task is a value-based pleasantness decision rather than a risky, ambiguous, or classic perceptual decision-making task focused on cue-reactivity. While the study does report group-level whole-brain task activation maps and parametrically relates BOLD to stimulus discriminability (ΔI), satisfying I6 and I7, it does not meet I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making relevant to the review) nor I5 (within-task contrasts explicitly matching risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts as defined). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: none ([])

This study meets all specified inclusion criteria: (I4) participants performed a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analog Risk Task) during fMRI; (I5) within-task contrasts are reported (choose win > choose inflate; outcome inflate > outcome explode); (I6) group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were conducted (permutation testing across the whole brain), even though no significant clusters survived correction; (I7) whole-brain analyses and ROI results are clearly described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical, includes within-task contrasts, and reports whole-brain analyses (so it is not ROI-only, seed/connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore I include this study for the review focused on task-evoked decision-making contrasts.

This study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps were reported and second-level whole-brain comparisons were performed) and I7 (results/coordinates reported in tables/figures and described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (while the study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task, the meta-analysis specifies risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks and this paper focuses on reinforcement learning/RPE processing rather than explicitly framed risky/ambiguous decision-making), and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrast of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making, e.g. "risky > safe", "ambiguity > non-ambiguous", or "hard > easy"; instead the primary contrasts are model-derived RPE parametric modulators and group comparisons of RPE). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only-without-task-effect, or non-empirical paper issues). Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to satisfy I4 and I5 required for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study does not address the review objective (fMRI cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards using visual stimuli) and does not report an fMRI task involving risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required. Although it collected task-based fMRI and performed group-level whole-brain activation analyses (satisfying I6) and reported whole-brain results in figures/tables (satisfying I7), it fails to meet I4 (task type: risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and I5 (at least one within/between-task contrast specifically related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

Excluded because the study does not address the review objective (meta-analysis of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Although this is an empirical fMRI study with participants performing a risky decision-making task (I4 met) and the authors ran whole-brain group-level analyses and reported whole-brain results/figures (I6 and I7 met), it does not report any within-task or between-task contrast directly related to risk (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk) required by I5. The primary reported fMRI contrasts concern conditioned-stimulus (relief vs. fear) cue responses and model-based ROI correlations, and no unmasked whole-brain risky>safe (or analogous) task contrast is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to visual drug or natural reward-related stimuli. Although the full text is complete and the paper employed task-based fMRI during an economic lottery (risky decision-making) task and reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (satisfying inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7), it examines risk-related decision-making and delay discounting rather than cue-reactivity to drug/natural reward visual cues. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore it must be excluded because it fails to address the review’s core topic (cue-reactivity to visual drug/natural reward cues).

This study collected fMRI during a risky gamble decision-making task (Experiment 3) using visual conditioned cues (fractals) and reports group-level, second-level voxelwise analyses. The authors tested within-task contrasts that index risky versus safe decisions within an interaction (decision × conditioned stimulus) and report activation coordinates (left amygdala) from the group analysis; they also provide whole-brain exploratory maps/coordinates (supplementary). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Note: the study uses monetary conditioned cues rather than drug cues, but it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I4–I7 as specified.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that implemented two perceptual decision-making tasks (criterion comparison and signal detection) with easy vs difficult conditions and parametric uncertainty modeling. The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM and searchlight MVPA results with cluster-corrected maps and Talairach coordinates (i.e., voxelwise whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). Contrasts and parametric regressors relate directly to perceptual decision difficulty/uncertainty (e.g., difficult > easy and parametric uncertainty), satisfying the perceptual-DM contrast requirement. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The article reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination) with RT and difficulty manipulations, satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts and analyses directly tied to perceptual decision-making (e.g., face > house contrasts, RT-bin analyses, difficulty/noise-level comparisons), satisfying I5. Analyses were performed with voxelwise, group-level GLMs and ANOVAs across the whole brain, and results are reported as statistical maps and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Exclusion decision rationale: This paper is an empirical fMRI study of risky and strategic decision-making and meets the methodological inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during risky/strategic decision tasks), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risky/uncertain choices, e.g., B-choice > A-choice and task contrasts across lotteries/stag-hunt/entry), I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with FWE correction), and I7 (reporting of whole-brain results with peak MNI coordinates and text/figures). However, it does NOT address the meta-analysis review objective (fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Because the study topic (decision-making/strategic uncertainty) does not match the review objective, it is excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based analyses (variance comparisons within preselected SPL/IPL ROIs) and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or standard within-task/between-task activation contrasts. Exclusion ID E3 applies. Inclusion: I4 is satisfied (human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task on ambiguous faces). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no reported within-task or between-task activation contrast maps related to perceptual decision-making) and I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps; results are ROI-based variance tests). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, DOI). Therefore the study fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and is excluded.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI experiment in human participants performing a decision-making task that manipulated objective vs. subjective uncertainty (certain 100:0 sequences vs. uncertain 80:20 sequences). It includes within-task contrasts (e.g., first-draw certain vs. baseline, certain vs. uncertain), group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses implemented in SPM with cluster-level correction, and results presented in tables/figures (Tables IV and Supporting Information). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, acquisition, preprocessing, analysis), Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during decision-making with uncertainty), I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures). It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study acquired task-based BOLD data while human youth performed a well-defined risky decision-making task (Cups Task) during scanning, satisfying I4. The analyses include within-task contrasts separating risky vs nonrisky choices and gain vs loss conditions (e.g., risky > nonrisky; condition contrasts), satisfying I5. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical analyses were conducted using FSL FLAME1 with cluster correction (Z>2.3, P<.05), and results are reported with anatomical localization and coordinates, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral and whole-brain fMRI), and discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity analyses. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making (gamble) task (I4). It includes within-task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (experimental gamble vs control gamble; high vs low probability; high vs low gain) (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (FLAME for within-group effects; OLS for between-group effects) with cluster-based thresholding and coordinates/tables/figures provided (I6,I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include within-task whole-brain task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and is included.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic object-reversal task involving uncertainty/ambiguity in reward-based decisions (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric modulation related to learning/uncertainty and decision phase (e.g., ‘learned’ > ‘not yet learned’ and parametric bins), satisfying I5. Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM2 with voxelwise mixed-effects models and whole-brain statistics used to define ROIs; results are reported with coordinates and figures (meets I6 and I7). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of decision-making fMRI studies targeting uncertainty/ambiguity.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (selection, speed/accuracy, confidence). Within-task contrasts (instruction, stimulus/perceptual judgment, confidence epochs; task > rest) are reported and used to define ROIs; whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are described (thresholded FWE-corrected maps) and unthresholded maps are available on NeuroVault. Coordinates for ROIs are provided. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (coordinates/maps reported). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI investigation of risky decision-making using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART). It meets the methodological inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing risky vs safe/prepump vs pre-cash-out), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses/searchlight and univariate contrast maps), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables). However, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective focused on cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli (i.e., the study examines risk-taking behavior, not reward cue-reactivity), so it is not eligible for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants made prospective mixed-gamble decisions involving risk and effort, satisfying the decision-making requirement. Specifically: I4 met — fMRI collected while participants performed risky/prospective decision-making tasks (mixed gambles with prospective effort and risk). I5 met — within-task contrasts/parametric regressors relate to prospective risk and effort magnitude and subjective-value (e.g., parametric modulation of prospective risk/effort; predicted acceptance probability regressors). I6 met — group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (GLMs, cluster-corrected maps) and unthresholded maps are available on NeuroVault. I7 met — whole-brain results are clearly described with MNI coordinates and supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported with cluster- and peak-level statistics and whole-brain GLM analyses) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is a probabilistic learning/confidence-reporting task, not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts mapping onto risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts such as “risky>safe”, “ambiguity>non-ambiguous”, or “hard>easy”; instead contrasts relate to confidence, surprise, and Bayesian updates). Exclusion criteria triggered: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete = false (full Methods, Results, and Discussion are present). Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to satisfy I4 and I5 required by the meta-analysis.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts including risky > sure and sure > risky), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported with whole-brain FWE correction), I7 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion IDs not met: none. Primary reason for exclusion: although the study satisfies the listed inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug- and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (no cue-reactivity, drug/natural reward, or visual cue paradigm). Therefore it is not relevant to the stated meta-analysis objective and is excluded on those grounds. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I4: the fMRI task is a passive slot-machine (participants press a button to start but make no risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decisions and there is no behavioral choice component). While the study includes a within-task contrast of uncertain reward anticipation > no-incentive anticipation (consistent with I5 ‘high uncertainty > low uncertainty’), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activations (I6) with acceptable reporting in text/tables/figures (I7), the lack of a decision-making element violates I4, and ALL inclusion criteria must be met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study used BOLD fMRI during an intertemporal choice (temporal discounting) task and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and contrasts (easy>control, hard>control, hard>easy). It therefore satisfies I5 (within-task contrasts including hard>easy), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps), and I7 (results clearly reported via figures/tables). However, it does not meet I4 because the task is an intertemporal/temporal discounting decision-making task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as specified by the inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I4 is not satisfied; other inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7) are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (dot-motion coherence). The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric analyses directly relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., inverse relationship/low-coherence > high-coherence effects, RT-BOLD regressions, correct vs incorrect contrasts). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise/statistical maps (surface-mapped group linear-trend analyses and ROI results derived from independent runs), with results described in text, figures, and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, and is empirical).

This study reports an fMRI investigation of risk-taking using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART) with human participants (heavy drinkers) performing a risky decision-making task. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to risk (e.g., mean color pump > mean white pump [risky > nonrisky], linear color pump > linear white pump [parametric risk], Explosions > Cashouts). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (FSL mixed-effects, cluster-based whole-brain correction) and results are presented in text, tables, and figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (categorization of multi-element visual arrays), with parametric contrasts of perceptual difficulty/uncertainty (mean- and variance-related uncertainty; e.g., proximity-to-bound, variability) reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (SPM8), with peaks/clusters and tables/figures described in the text (cluster-corrected results and coordinates). Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual difficulty/uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported via tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human participants performing perceptual decision-making (random-dot motion) and a rule-based decision task (Sudoku), meeting I4. It includes within-task contrasts and parametric regressors related to perceptual difficulty/uncertainty (e.g., task > control, hard/low-coherence effects, uncertainty-level regressions), meeting I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FLAME; FDR/FWE thresholds) with whole-brain statistical maps described in text and figures, meeting I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a multi-step gambling task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (quota-severity and strategy-optimization contrasts tied to risky vs. EV-based choices) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates). Thus all inclusion criteria for risky/decision-making fMRI studies are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (visual motion direction discrimination). It includes within-task parametric contrasts modulated by motion coherence (i.e., perceptual difficulty; equivalent to “low coherence > high coherence” type effects) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level permutation t-tests, cluster-level FWE correction) with maps and peak coordinates. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Although the overall meta-analysis objective mentions reward cue-reactivity, the provided inclusion criteria focus on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making: criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a perceptual decision (face discrimination) with within-task manipulations (evidence vs. noise; reward-bias vs. neutral) and ROI-based GLM/ANOVA analyses, so it meets I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision task) and I5 (within-task contrasts relating to perceptual difficulty/reward). However, the paper reports ROI time-course analyses (pIPS, PRR, FFA, etc.) and does not present or report group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables for whole-brain effects. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on E3 because the required whole-brain, group-level activation maps are not reported.

This fMRI study involved human participants making explicit choices about pronoun referents under conditions of ambiguity and risk (e.g., Undetermined vs Directly Determined, Gender-Neutral vs Gender-Biased, Indirectly Determined vs Directly Determined), satisfying the requirement for an ambiguous decision-making task (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to ambiguity/risk in referent assignment (I5). Analyses used group-level, whole-brain SPM5 random-effects voxelwise models and report whole-brain results and coordinate tables (I6,I7). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for ambiguous decision-making contrasts and provides whole-brain activation data suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a monetary/probabilistic reward task that manipulates uncertainty (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and reward magnitude. The authors report within-task contrasts explicitly modeling reward uncertainty (e.g., high uncertainty [50%] vs low/no uncertainty [100%]) and other contrasts (magnitude, value, prediction error). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM second-level ANOVAs with FDR/FWE correction and results reported in tables/figures/text. Full article includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I4 (human fMRI task involving risk/ambiguity), I5 (within-task contrasts related to uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI during the cups risky decision-making task (I4). It includes within-task contrasts related to risk and outcomes (e.g., risky > safe; win > loss) and between-group contrasts (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with GRF-corrected thresholds and two-sample t-tests (I6), and whole-brain results are described in text, figures and tables (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, and original empirical task-based fMRI data are reported. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria; include in meta-analysis of task-evoked whole-brain risky decision-making fMRI data.

This study is a human fMRI investigation of perceptual decision making (random-dot motion task) that includes hard>easy (low coherence>high coherence) contrasts and reports group-level whole-brain results with coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (perceptual contrast: hard>easy/low coherence>high coherence), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported in tables/coordinates). However, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (study concerns perceptual decision making, not reward cue-reactivity). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded due to lack of relevance to the review objective (does not investigate drug/natural reward cue-reactivity).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: (1) It acquired fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (monetary lotteries) (I4); (2) It reports within-task contrasts related to risk, including comparisons of risky > safe choices and parametric modulation by probability (I5); (3) Analyses included group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with FDR thresholding and reported whole-brain results (I6); (4) Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task whole-brain activations, and is empirical fMRI work in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Risky Gains Task (risky decision-making), satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risky versus safe decisions and group-by-decision effects (e.g., risky > safe, and post-loss risk behavior), satisfying I5. Although primary hypothesis testing was restricted to an a priori limbic mask, the manuscript indicates voxel-wise analyses and presents whole-brain patterns of task activation and group differences in the Supplementary Figures ( Supp. Figs 1-3 ), meeting I6 and I7 (whole-brain results acceptable in supplementary figures). The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and is an original empirical report. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Although this study reports a human fMRI experiment using a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts and relevant perceptual difficulty contrasts/parametric modulators, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual difficulty/conformity), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps reported), I7 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 are lacking ([]). However, the study topic is incompatible with the review objective (no drug/natural reward cue-reactivity; instead reputation, conformity, and shock anticipation), so it is excluded on topical grounds. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of dynamic learning/predictive inference and representational changes (uncertainty, latent states) using a sequential inference task. It does not investigate drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, nor does it implement a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task contrast required by the meta-analysis. Specifically, inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. The paper does report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight RSA, cluster-corrected maps) and reports whole-brain results in figures/tables, satisfying I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a sequential virtual foraging task that entails probabilistic (risky) decisions between foraging and waiting. The paper reports within-task, task-evoked contrasts and parametric modulators tied to risk-related decision variables (e.g., probability of foraging success, value differences of foraging vs. waiting, uncertainties, discrepancies). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests) are reported with cluster-level FWE correction and peak MNI coordinates, fulfilling the requirement that whole-brain results be available (coordinates and figures/tables provided). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that implemented a risky/ambiguous decision-making paradigm (urn gambles) and collected task-evoked BOLD during observation of draws. The authors report within-task parametric contrasts related to belief updating, value updating, and expectancy violation (i.e., ambiguity/risk-related effects) and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with cluster-level FWE correction; results are presented as activation maps and tables. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and the paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: (I4) It is an fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making task that manipulates risk and ambiguity (Card-Deck paradigm). (I5) It reports within-task contrasts relevant to risky/ambiguous decision-making (e.g., decision under risk > decision under ambiguity; bet choice > safe choice) and between-group contrasts. (I6) Analyses were group-level, whole-brain (random-effects ANOVA, voxelwise threshold p<0.001 with cluster correction) and (I7) whole-brain results and coordinates are reported in tables and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: the paper does not report only ROI, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts; whole-brain task activations are presented. Although the meta-analysis focus is on reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, this paper examines monetary reward anticipation/visual card stimuli in pathological gamblers (relevant reward-cue domain), so it is appropriate for inclusion under the provided criteria.

The full text is complete and empirical. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps were reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is value-based cost–benefit accept/reject decisions, not explicitly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required) and I5 (does not report contrasts framed as risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts such as 'risky > safe', 'ambiguity > non-ambiguous', or the specific perceptual contrasts requested). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I4 and I5 required for this review’s focus on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (and on drug/natural reward cue-reactivity visual stimuli).

This study meets the review inclusion criteria: (1) It used task-based fMRI in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) (I4). (2) It reports within-task contrasts directly related to risk (e.g., high-risk (25%) > low-risk (75%), 25/75 risk/reward > control, 25/75 > 50/50) (I5). (3) The methods describe group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses and generation of contrast images; although ROI results are emphasized, the paper explicitly states that whole-brain analyses were conducted (I6). (4) Results include coordinates and descriptions of peak voxels in tables/figures (Table 3 and Figure 2), satisfying the allowance for coordinate reporting (I7). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting without whole-brain results) are evident based on the text provided. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked fMRI risk-related contrasts.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a Paper-Scissors-Rock decision-making task involving probabilistic (preferred/even/worst) choices, which constitutes risky/ambiguous decision-making. It reports within-task contrasts (preferred, even, worst responses) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (linear mixed effects on PSC values) with multiple-comparison cluster correction; results are reported in tables and figures with coordinates. Thus it satisfies I4 (task-based risky/ambiguous decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported as tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts without whole-brain task effect, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study acquired task-based whole-brain data while participants performed decision-making tasks (delay discounting and probability discounting). It includes within-task contrasts directly related to risk/probability (probability option > fixed option) and delay (delay option > no-delay option). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses were performed and reported with cluster-level FWE correction; results are presented in figures/tables (satisfies reporting of whole-brain results). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, only between-group contrasts without task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Stoplight Task (a risky decision-making paradigm) during scanning, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (Go vs baseline; Stop vs baseline; Stop (safe) vs Go (risky); and condition comparisons mother vs adult), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are conducted and reported (whole-brain t-tests, cluster-correction thresholds) with results presented in tables and figures, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study meets the review inclusion criteria: (I4) participants underwent fMRI while performing a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game); (I5) contrasts of interest include risky vs safe decisions (go vs stop) and peer/parent contrasts; (I6) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-FWE corrected whole-brain results and NeuroVault repository); (I7) whole-brain results are described in text/figures and made available. No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to connectivity-only analyses (E4) — although PPI is reported, whole-brain task activation maps are also provided — not only between-group contrasts (E5), and it is an empirical fMRI study (not E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses of a temporally-extended probabilistic categorization (ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) task with parametric contrasts and tables of coordinates, it does NOT address the meta-analysis topic of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Therefore it does not meet the review’s topical requirement and cannot be included. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (n=24) that collected whole-brain task-evoked BOLD data while participants performed a financial decision-making task under risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric modulators directly related to risky decision-making (probability weighting, weighted lottery value, sure-win magnitude) and contrasts (MESSAGE vs NO MESSAGE; follow vs ignore advice) tied to risk-related processing. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (t-maps, cluster thresholds, tables/figures). Results are described with figures and coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although this study used fMRI during a probabilistic two-armed bandit decision-making task (meets I4) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates (meets I6 and I7), it does not report at least one within-task or between-task contrast explicitly related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, risky > safe). The fMRI analyses focus on parametric modulators of expected value (Q) at choice and reward/RPE at outcome, but do not present contrasts that map onto the risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts required by I5. Therefore I5 is not met and the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study satisfies methodological inclusion criteria: I4 (human fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk, e.g., accept > reject and other decision-value contrasts), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with clusterwise FDR correction), and I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and supplemental material). However, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward–related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli: the task involves monetary gambles and adaptive decision policies rather than cue-reactivity to visual drug or natural reward stimuli. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet the review’s topical requirement (does not examine cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards using visual stimuli).

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Although it reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I6) and presents whole-brain results clearly in text/figures (I7), it does not investigate cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards and therefore does not meet the review’s topical scope. Additionally, it does not provide an explicit within-task whole-brain contrast framed as risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (I4 and I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a risk-taking decision-making task (anticipatory risky choices), with within-task conditions including high-risk and low-risk, reward and loss (satisfying I4/I5). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with familywise-error whole-brain correction and whole-brain clusters (satisfying I6/I7). Results include whole-brain contrasts (group, group×valence, feedback main effects) and coordinates/ROI follow-ups; it does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the article meets all specified inclusion criteria for whole-brain risky decision-making fMRI studies and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game) in participants performing risky vs. cautious choices, satisfying I4. The authors report within-task contrasts (Decision Trial − Directed Trial; analyses of activation preceding risky responses) directly related to risky decision-making, satisfying I5. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level regression maps using permutation testing, with results reported as cluster tables and coordinates, satisfying I6 and I7. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study is an fMRI experiment of a six-armed restless bandit task with monetary gains/losses and model-based regressors for risk, estimation uncertainty, and unexpected uncertainty. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results and parametric contrasts relating to risk/uncertainty. However, the meta-analysis objective is fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli; this study does not examine cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards (it uses monetary outcomes and a decision-making task rather than cue-reactivity paradigms). Therefore it does not address the review objective and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not address the review objective (fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual cues) and does not employ the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported) and I7 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task type — study used probabilistic reversal learning, not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task as specified) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts of the form ‘risky>safe’, ‘ambiguous>non-ambiguous’, or ‘hard>easy’; instead parametric PE regressors were used). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that acquired whole-brain BOLD data while participants performed a risky/ambiguous decision-making task (lotteries with ambiguous vs nonambiguous gambles). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to ambiguity (ambiguous > nonambiguous) and parametric effects of second-order uncertainty (entropy), and uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with cluster- and small-volume-corrected results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Although this study meets the methodological inclusion criteria for the decision-making fMRI meta-analysis (I4–I7: it used fMRI during a risky decision-making task, reported a within-task contrast (Dishonest vs Honest) that maps onto risky>safe, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported with standard thresholds/coordinates), it does NOT address the stated review objective of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The experimental paradigm concerns dishonest economic choices and outcome processing, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards evoked by visual cues. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the review topic, despite meeting inclusion criteria I4–I7.

This fMRI study is an instrumental probabilistic reward- and punishment-based reinforcement learning task in depressed and control participants. It does include group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (satisfying I6) and reports whole-brain results in the text/tables (satisfying I7). However, it does not meet the primary task-domain inclusion criteria: the task is a reinforcement learning/associative learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (criteria I4 and I5). The reported contrasts are reward vs neutral, punishment vs neutral, and prediction-error regressors, not contrasts such as “risky > safe”, “ambiguity > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), analyses are task-evoked (not resting-state/connectivity-only), and the paper is an empirical study. Full text appears complete. Therefore I exclude because I4 and I5 are not met.

This study reports a human fMRI experiment in which participants performed a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains) during BOLD acquisition (satisfying I4). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices and punished versus non-punished outcomes (satisfying I5). They conducted and report group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (with thresholding and cluster criteria) in addition to ROI analyses, and present whole-brain results in tables and figures (satisfying I6 and I7). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article text appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met: the paper does not report only ROI or connectivity results, nor is it non-empirical. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for decision-making fMRI contrasts and is included.

This study meets the methodological inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4: fMRI during a risky decision-making task), includes within-task contrasts related to risk/acceptance (I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps with coordinates and cluster-level inference (I6, I7). However, it does NOT address the stated meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual cues: the task involves monetary mixed gambles (decision-making about gains/losses) rather than visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. No exclusion criteria (E3, E4, E5, E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded on the basis of topical mismatch with the review objective (not a cue-reactivity study).

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG-fMRI study of perceptual decision-making and confidence (random-dot motion task) with whole-brain group-level activation maps. However, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli: no drug or natural reward cue exposure, no cue-reactivity paradigm, and no contrasts targeting reward-cue reactivity. Regarding the inclusion criteria: it satisfies I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). It does not satisfy I5 because the reported contrasts focus on confidence-related parametric modulation and EEG-informed regressors rather than perceptual difficulty contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence) or a perceptual task>control contrast relevant for perceptual-DM inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded for not addressing the review objective and for failing to provide the required perceptual-contrast (I5).

The manuscript reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an ambiguous social decision-making task (morphed faces requiring probabilistic emotion judgments). It includes within-task contrasts directly tied to ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (e.g., final decision: last face > previous faces; blocks with faces increasing in happiness or fear > baseline). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain FWE-corrected analyses and tables/ROIs are presented). The full text provides introduction, methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and analysis), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Although this study used whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI analyses (I6) and reported whole-brain results in figures/tables (I7), it does not address the stated meta-analysis objective of reward-related cue-reactivity to visual drug/natural cues. The task is a reinforcement-learning Paper-Scissors-Rock decision task in cocaine-dependent patients rather than a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting drug or natural reward visual stimuli. Therefore the study does not meet key inclusion criteria: I4 (task type: risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making as framed by the review) and I5 (a within-task contrast explicitly indexing risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making such as “risky>safe” or “ambiguity>non-ambiguity”). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level contrasts of probabilistic/rule-based decision-making (meets I4, I5, I6, I7), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. The task used neutral object cues and monetary incentives rather than drug/natural reward cues; therefore it does not match the review topic and is excluded on that basis. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: none of I4–I7 (but study fails to address the meta-analysis topical scope). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual trajectory prediction and computational/modeling of dynamic vs statistical predictions. Although it meets several methodological inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI (I4: fMRI during a perceptual decision task; I5: task-related within-task parametric contrasts; I6: group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses; I7: whole-brain results reported), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). The experimental stimuli and aims concern trajectory extrapolation and computational model specialization, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to address the review objective/relevant population/phenomenon of interest.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults using a gambling task that is a risky decision-making paradigm. It reports within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making (e.g., decisions after Norisk vs Riskwin; Risk vs Norisk; accepts vs rejects) and links neural activation to behavior. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with reported MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected thresholds (tables/figures described), and whole-brain results are presented alongside ROI analyses. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical constraints).

This is an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (satisfies I6 and I7). However, the experimental paradigm is a predictive-inference spatial learning task that manipulates surprise, relative uncertainty, and incidental reward; it is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as required by I4. The reported contrasts are computational regressors (CPP, RU, reward) and region-wise effects related to adaptive learning, not explicit risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts of the form required by I5 (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task), includes within-task contrasts comparing advantageous vs disadvantageous (risky vs safe) deck selections, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (within-group whole-brain analyses thresholded and corrected, reported in Methods and Results). These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task), with within-task parametric contrasts related to risk (pump number) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps (cluster-corrected) reported in figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, permitting verification of task, contrasts, and whole-brain analyses. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric modulation related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study meets the review inclusion criteria: (1) It performed fMRI while participants completed a risky decision task (laboratory and smartphone risky decision tasks) satisfying I4. (2) Neural analyses included within-task task-related contrasts/regressors tied to risky decision-making (expected value and reward prediction error correlates linked to choices/outcomes), satisfying I5. (3) Group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported/displayed (main effects images at uncorrected P<.001 and reported activations including medial PFC), indicating whole-brain analyses were performed, satisfying I6. (4) Whole-brain results are presented as figures/images (acceptable per I7). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical).

This study used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task that probes decision-making under uncertainty (probabilistic/ambiguous feedback). The authors report within-task contrasts (lose-shift vs other feedback conditions) that index decision-related behavioral adjustment and present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected whole-brain analyses and reported cluster peaks). Whole-brain activation maps and peaks are described in the text and figures/SI. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. Thus it meets criteria for an fMRI task probing ambiguous/risky decision-making, provides relevant within-task contrasts, and reports whole-brain group-level results.

This is an fMRI study in human Parkinson's patients that used an explicit risky decision-making task during BOLD imaging (task-based fMRI) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. It includes a within-task parametric regressor for ‘Gamble Risk’ and reports task-related contrasts and interactions (Group, Medication, Valence) with whole-brain SPM results, tables, and figures. The methods describe preprocessing, first-level modelling with a parametric regressor, and a flexible factorial group-level analysis with FDR correction, fulfilling whole-brain statistical map requirements. Therefore it meets I4 (task fMRI of risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric risk contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study in healthy human adults using the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to risk (risky > safe; punishment feedback > risky) and additional contrasts examining effects of punishment on subsequent choices. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are described with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster correction (P < 0.001, cluster-level), and whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical restriction).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making paradigm). The authors present within-task contrasts related to expected value, ambiguity/high vs low value, and prediction errors, and they report voxelwise, group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses (thresholded maps and cluster-corrected results). These outputs satisfy the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) apply.

Although this study meets the methodological inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI (I4: human fMRI during a perceptual 2AFC task; I5: within-task/model-based contrasts related to perceptual decision processes; I6: group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed; I7: whole-brain results reported in text/figures), it does not address the meta-analysis objective. The review specifically targets fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, whereas this study used olfactory stimuli and investigated temporal evidence integration in olfactory perception (not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues or visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are met. Therefore the article is excluded on topical grounds (does not address review objective: not drug/natural reward cue-reactivity and not visual modality).

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adults performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task), includes within-task contrasts assessing parametric modulation by pump number (risk level), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected) with results described in text, figures, and effect-size maps. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level activation maps (SPM random-effects) and reports task contrasts (weather prediction > perceptual-motor control). However, the experimental paradigm is probabilistic category learning (weather prediction) and not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required by I4 and I5; the contrasts are not of the form required (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5 despite meeting I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This article reports an fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making task (two-choice monetary risk-taking task) and includes within-task contrasts (e.g., risky vs safe during cue, choice, and feedback phases, risky win vs safe, risky win vs risky loss). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps conducted in AFNI with cluster-correction and coordinates/tables reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study involved human participants performing decision-making tasks under uncertainty (diagnosis/prescription vs naming), manipulating diagnosticity (high vs low) to index ambiguity/uncertainty, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to diagnostic uncertainty/diagnosticity (e.g., foreperiod > high-diagnosticity first stimulus; epoch and diagnosticity ANOVAs), meeting I5. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with random-effects inference and FWE correction and peak MNI coordinates reported, satisfying I6 and I7. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (tactile spatial pattern discrimination) during scanning (I4). The authors report within-task contrasts/analyses related to perceptual decision difficulty (parametric modulation by pattern quality / decision difficulty; equivalent to hard>easy contrasts) (I5). Data were analyzed with a group-level random-effects GLM and results report task-related areas across the whole brain (corrected P values, lists of regions), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps; results are reported in text/figures/tables (I6, I7). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures) is provided here and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of financial risky decision making (BIAS task). It includes within-task contrasts directly comparing risky versus riskless choices (stock vs. bond) and outcome contrasts (gain vs. loss) relevant to risky decision-making. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and statistical maps (group statistical maps, global thresholds, small-volume corrections, and cluster thresholds are described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text provided contains introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition and analysis), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli). Although it is an empirical fMRI study of risky decision making and includes task contrasts and within-subject threat vs safe contrasts, it focuses on anticipatory anxiety induced by threat-of-shock and value coding during risky choices, not on cue-reactivity to reward cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making task) and I5 (within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (the target analyses relevant to the meta-analysis—group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps of reward-cue reactivity—are not provided for reward-cue contrasts; decision-related value analyses were ROI-restricted). Exclusion criteria (E3–E6) do not apply. Therefore EXCLUDE due to lack of relevance to the review objective and missing whole-brain reward-cue task maps.

The study does not address the review objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. It reports an fMRI reversal learning task and analyses of prediction-error (PE) signals in the ventral striatum and their relation to life stress and fluid intelligence. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects analysis was performed) and I7 (whole-brain results referenced/shown in supplementary materials). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 and I5 — the task is a reinforcement/reversal learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task with contrasts such as “risky > safe” or “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, and no such risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts are reported. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED for not meeting the domain-specific inclusion criteria of the meta-analysis.

Although this study meets the fMRI methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with contrasts probing outcome uncertainty/ambiguity), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of reward-related cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous/risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to ambiguity/uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Inclusion criteria not met relative to the review objective: the study does not investigate drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (topic mismatch). Therefore it is excluded from this reward-cue-reactivity meta-analysis despite satisfying technical fMRI criteria.

Excluded because the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. This paper investigates novelty-driven exploration and reinforcement learning in a four-armed bandit task using neutral landscape images, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task under uncertainty), I5 (within-task contrasts related to decision-making/novelty bonuses), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 are unmet, but the study fails to address the review’s topical objective (drug/natural reward cue-reactivity). Exclusion criteria applied: none of E3–E6. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study using a perceptual decision-making task (animal detection) with a motivation manipulation (monetary incentive) and includes appropriate within-task contrasts (motivated > neutral; stimulus+decision > implicit baseline). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) and provides results in the text and ROI-corrected follow-ups. It is an empirical, complete full text with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects).

Although the study meets the provided task-based fMRI inclusion criteria (it used the BART risky decision-making task in human participants and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. The meta-analysis objective requires studies of visual cue-reactivity; this study examines decision-making/risk processing after wins/losses rather than neural responses to visual reward-related cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (risky decision-making fMRI), I5 (within-task contrasts / parametric modulation of risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met relative to the review objective: study does not assess visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards (so does not address the review objective). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task based on the Game of Dice Task with explicit probabilities and incentives (decision-making under risk). It reports within-task contrasts (activation condition A vs high-level control B and A vs C) directly testing information-based/risk processing. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 and significant activations are reported with cluster statistics and MNI/Talairach coordinates (tables and figures). Thus it satisfies I4 (task-based fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast: experimental risk > control), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables and textual description). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky/uncertain decision-making task (BIAS), includes within-task contrasts related to risk/uncertainty (parametric modulation of uncertainty; bond vs. stock choices/risk-avoidant vs. risk-seeking), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, whole-brain thresholding and cluster reports/tables). Results are described in text/tables and constitute task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided).
