Study is an fMRI experiment of decision-making about source preference and ambiguity aversion, not a drug or natural reward cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (does not address review objective). Based on available information: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-making) and I5 (within-task contrasts like familiar>unfamiliar and risk vs ambiguity contrasts) appear satisfied. There is no clear evidence of group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps reported, nor full reporting of whole-brain results (I6 and I7 cannot be confirmed). Because I6 (whole-brain evidence) cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, I exclude the study. Exclusion IDs met: none confirmed. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I6, I7. Full text incomplete: true.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human adults performing a risky decision-making gambling task (Modified Cups Task), satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly comparing decisions following wins vs losses (e.g., Riskloss > Riskwin and Riskwin > Riskloss) and feedback-related contrasts, satisfying I5. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM results with cluster correction and reported coordinates/figures, satisfying I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity- or resting-state-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and the paper is empirical fMRI data in healthy adults (not E6). Full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making Wheel of Fortune task (I4 satisfied) and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and figures (I6 and I7 satisfied). However, the analyses reported in this paper focus on feedback (reward receipt) contrasts (Win > No Win) rather than decision-phase risk contrasts (e.g., risky > safe). The inclusion criterion I5 requires at least one within-task or between-task contrast specifically related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making; no risky-vs-safe or equivalent decision-phase whole-brain contrast is reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5 (risk-related contrast absent).

Does not address the review objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Although this is an fMRI study of risky decision-making with whole-brain task-evoked maps and contrasts (skewed vs symmetric; positive vs negative skew) and reports group-level voxelwise results, it investigates monetary gambles rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Therefore it is not conceptually eligible for a meta-analysis focused on reward cue-reactivity. Full text is complete.

The study does not address the review objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and does not include the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise analyses reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined) and I5 (no within-task contrasts corresponding to risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or perceptual hard>easy; reported contrasts are gain/loss/omission vs neutral and PE parametric modulators). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria and does not address the specific review objective.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (IGT) and reported task contrasts (IGT > control), satisfying I4 and I5. However, all neuroimaging analyses were restricted to an anatomically-defined VMPFC ROI (and group-level inference was performed within that mask); no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group task-activation map is reported. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this paper meets the technical inclusion criteria for risky/ambiguous decision-making fMRI studies (I4: fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision task; I5: within-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity such as SV-related regressors and ambiguity>risk contrasts; I6: group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected thresholds; I7: whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. The study examines monetary decision-making (risk and ambiguity) and valuation processes, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered. Therefore, despite satisfying I4–I7, the study is excluded because it does not address the review’s substantive objective (drug/natural reward cue-reactivity).

Exclusion IDs met: none (E3, E4, E5, E6 do not apply). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-making tasks), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/probability/regret), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (results reported in figures/tables/text). Inclusion IDs not met: the study does NOT address the meta-analysis topical objective — it is not a cue-reactivity study of drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli (topic mismatch). Therefore excluded based on failure to meet the review objective despite satisfying I4–I7. Full text completeness: full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reported coordinate tables, it does not address the meta-analysis topic of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The experiment is a reversal-learning task comparing certain (2-choice) vs uncertain (4-choice) response outcomes and contrasts unexpected non-reinforcement vs expected reinforcement; it does not present drug or natural reward cues or cue-reactivity contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task analyses reported) and I7 (results reported as tables/figures/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met for the purposes of this review: I4 (task is not a drug/natural reward cue-reactivity task as specified by the review objective) and I5 (no within- or between-task contrast that reflects drug/natural reward cue-reactivity such as cue > control). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a mixed-lottery risky decision-making task (Lottery Choice Task), satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric analyses related to probability/risk (e.g., linear and quadratic probability regressors, age × probability interactions) constituting task-relevant risk contrasts, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain 3-way ANOVA and model-based whole-brain maps with significance thresholds and cluster corrections), satisfying I6. Results are reported in the full text (with supplementary tables/figures), satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, and it reports whole-brain task activation maps; it is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of task-evoked, whole-brain risky decision-making fMRI studies.

Although this fMRI study involves a perceptual decision-making task and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results with parametric contrasts of coherence (meeting I4, I5, I6, and I7), it does NOT address the meta-analysis topic of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study investigates motion/color perceptual decision-making and attention, with no reward-cue or drug-related cues or contrasts reported. Therefore it does not meet the review objective and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply.

The study reports fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with volatile (uncertain) vs stable phases—i.e., an uncertainty/ambiguity decision-making paradigm. The authors provide group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise model-based activation maps (RPE and trial-wise learning rate) and report whole-brain results and tables/figures. They also report a psychological contrast (learning-rate-modulation trials vs nonlearning trials) akin to high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplemental references).

Although this study includes fMRI during a risky decision-making task (BART) with whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (active > passive) and reports voxelwise results, it does not address the stated meta-analysis objective of reward-related cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. The task involves monetary reward and decision processes rather than visual cue-reactivity contrasts to drug/natural rewards, and no visual cue-reactivity contrasts are reported. Therefore it is not appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of cue-reactivity to visual reward cues.

This fMRI study conducted whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise analyses while human participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task involving uncertainty and changing reward contingencies (i.e., decision-making under risk/ambiguity). The paper reports group-level contrasts and parametric modulators (learning rate, expected value, prediction error) correlated with BOLD activity and provides voxelwise results (Figures/tables) and ROI-corrected statistics. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (task during fMRI), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric task effects related to decision-making under uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (results reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This empirical human fMRI study used a perceptual categorization task with an uncertainty (opt-out) response, reporting within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., uncertainty > correct, correct > uncertainty, near vs far, parametric distance-to-bound modulators analogous to hard>easy). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-thresholded maps and coordinate tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task perceptual decision contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses (corrected whole-brain maps reported in tables/figures) of a probabilistic reversal-learning (PRL) task in schizophrenia vs controls. It satisfies I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). However, it does NOT meet I4 or I5: the task is a reinforcement-based probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as specified by the inclusion examples, and the reported contrasts (lose-shift > win-stay, final error > error) are not contrasts of risky vs safe, ambiguous vs non-ambiguous, or hard vs easy perceptual decisions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5 not met) despite meeting I6 and I7.

Although this study meets the methodological inclusion criteria for the review (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task with within-task contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paradigm manipulated monetary motivation in an animal-detection task rather than presenting drug or natural reward cues (e.g., food, drug-related images) for cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered (whole-brain results reported, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Therefore I exclude the study for not meeting the review’s topical objective (drug/natural reward cue-reactivity).

Does not address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual stimuli. The study is an fMRI investigation of sequential gambling/decision-making (risk) and network dynamics, not cue-reactivity to drug/natural reward cues. It does, however, meet the provided imaging decision-making inclusion criteria (I4–I7): human fMRI during risky decision-making task (I4), within-task contrasts related to risk (parametric 'cumulative gambling', stop probability) (I5), group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported (I6), and coordinates/figures provided (I7). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Because the study does not address the stated review objective (reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), it is excluded.

This is an empirical, group-level fMRI study in healthy adults using a risky decision-making task (104 mixed gambles) with participants accepting/rejecting gambles. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric analyses related to anticipation of gains vs losses and neural correlates of loss aversion, using random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded, reported in figures/tables). Multimodal whole-brain analyses (fMRI, VBM, SBM) and tables/figures present the whole-brain results. Therefore it meets the review’s focus on fMRI task-evoked whole-brain activation for reward-related cue-reactivity in a risky decision-making paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

While this full-text reports an fMRI perceptual decision-making task with appropriate within-task contrasts (high vs low coherence), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis, and reported coordinates, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (perceptual decision-making fMRI task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making: high>low and low>high coherence), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), I7 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. Because the study does not investigate reward-related cue-reactivity (topic mismatch with review objective), it is excluded. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (learning/choice between sure 20¢ and risky 0/40¢ options), satisfying I4. The paper includes within-task contrasts and analyses directly related to risk (e.g., comparisons of risky versus sure trials, prediction-error regressors tied to risk-sensitive choice), satisfying I5. A group-level whole-brain SPM2 analysis was performed and reported (familywise error-corrected threshold p<0.05), with identified clusters and coordinates, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans using a sequential risk-taking task (boxes with a hidden ‘devil’), satisfying the risky decision-making requirement. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric analyses comparing contexts and outcomes (e.g., Self_Optimum, Self_Non-optimum, Self_Devil, Computer_Optimum, etc.), and Context×Outcome F-contrasts, meeting the requirement for at least one within-task contrast related to risky decision-making. Data were analyzed at the group level using SPM8 with second-level random-effects analyses and whole-brain voxelwise results reported with MNI coordinates and cluster/FWE thresholds, fulfilling whole-brain evidence reporting (and acceptable reporting in tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates) is present. Thus I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This study used an fMRI serial reaction time paradigm to examine sequential predictive learning (behavioral RTs and model-based regressors). It reports group-level whole-brain analyses and supplementary tables/figures (satisfying I6 and I7). However, it does not implement or report contrasts of interest for the review (no risky, ambiguity, or perceptual decision-making contrasts such as “hard>easy” or “low coherence>high coherence”); therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI in human subjects performing a risky decision-making domino game (meets I4). It also reports within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., nonmatch > match; show > no-show), satisfying I5. However, the MRI acquisition covered only four functional slices centered on the amygdala (not whole-brain), and analyses focus on anatomically defined amygdala ROIs and slice-limited GLMs. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or coordinate tables/figures that reflect whole-brain results. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain evidence) and does not meet the acceptable alternative in I7. This violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only / no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Although this study meets the listed decision-making fMRI criteria (I4–I7), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. Specifically, the paper reports a longitudinal fMRI decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) with monetary rewards and contrasts such as risky > safe, includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (tables of clusters/coordinates), and reports results accordingly. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (risky > safe contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met relative to the review objective: study does not examine cue-reactivity to drug-related or natural reward visual cues (i.e., it does not present visual drug/natural reward cues or measure cue-elicited reactivity). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered by the methods or reporting. Therefore, excluded because the study does not address the specific review question of visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards.

This paper reports an fMRI study in humans performing a well-defined risky decision-making task (loss aversion/coin-flip economic gambles), satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts and parametric regressors for gains and losses (gain-related and loss-related BOLD), plus behavioral correlations and group contrasts, satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise with cluster correction and reported voxelwise results (figures/tables/supplement), satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to connectivity/resting-state (E4), and they report unmasked whole-brain task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E5); the paper is empirical (E6 not met). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The study does not meet the decision-making task and whole-brain reporting requirements. Exclusion ID met: E3 (reports only ROI fMRI results with no whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (fMRI was conducted during a Monetary Incentive Delay task probing reward anticipation/outcome, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (reported contrasts are win vs no-win/reward outcomes rather than risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrasts), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are presented; analyses focus on ROI beta extractions). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded for this meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of urgent vs. evaluative behavior in driving (risk decision-making), not a cue-reactivity study of drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Therefore it does not address the stated meta-analysis objective (reward-related cue-reactivity). It does, however, meet the technical inclusion criteria for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making: I4 (fMRI during risky decision task: urgent/evaluative driving tasks), I5 (within-task contrast urgent > evaluative reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected thresholds reported), and I7 (results reported with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because the primary review objective is reward-related cue-reactivity (drug/natural rewards) and this study does not investigate reward cue-reactivity, it is excluded.

Full text is complete. This study is excluded because it does not provide a within-task or between-task contrast related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (I5 not met). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (an fMRI was conducted while participants performed a decision-making guessing task under uncertainty), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps/analyses are reported), and I7 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables described in text). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). Therefore the study fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I5) and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of exploratory/exploitative decision-making using a four-armed bandit task. Although it meets the listed decision-making fMRI inclusion criteria (I4–I7: task-based fMRI, within-task contrast exploratory>exploitative, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported, and results presented in figures/tables), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. The task uses abstract point rewards and decision processes rather than presentation of drug or natural reward cues. Therefore it fails the overarching requirement to study cue-reactivity to (drug/natural) visual cues and must be excluded.

This study meets the decision-making fMRI criteria: (I4) it acquired task-based fMRI during decision-making (delay discounting and risk-sensitivity tasks). (I5) It reports within-task contrasts related to risky/temporal decision-making (choice vs baseline, categorical chosen-variable regressors, parametric subjective-value regressors). (I6) It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded and cluster-corrected via permutation testing). (I7) Whole-brain results are described in text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, reports task activation maps, is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with incidental object encoding, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I4 (task type) and I5 (within-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). Although the paper reports task fMRI and refers to whole-brain results (so a whole-brain group analysis may exist), the required task contrasts for this meta-analysis are absent. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports whole-brain fMRI in human subjects performing a risky decision-making task (monetary gambles) with within-task parametric contrasts and group-level voxelwise analyses, satisfying I4, I5, I6, and I7. However, the study investigates probability weighting in monetary gamble evaluation—not cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli, which is the stated meta-analysis objective. Therefore it does not address the review question and is out of scope. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study includes a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty) and a passive picture-viewing task of appetitive food images. It reports a within-task contrast of reward>punishment from the reversal learning paradigm and positive>neutral for picture viewing, satisfying the requirement for a contrast related to decision-making/reward. Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed using FLAME with nonparametric permutation testing and threshold-free cluster enhancement; group-level contrasts and peak coordinates are reported, indicating whole-brain task-evoked maps were produced. Results are presented with coordinates and corrected statistics. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Although this study meets the decision-making fMRI criteria (I4-I7), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports an fMRI two-choice prediction task with an aversive interoceptive (breathing) manipulation in methamphetamine users and healthy controls, not visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Therefore it is conceptually outside the review scope. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (task-based fMRI on risky/ambiguous decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to error-rate/risk/uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met for the review objective: study does not examine cue-reactivity to visual reward-related stimuli and thus does not address the primary review question. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered by the study's reporting. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making task (50/50 monetary gambles) with in-scanner task performance — satisfying I4. The authors report within-task contrasts (novel vs familiar prime) that are directly related to modulation of subsequent risky choices and perform a regression linking this contrast to percent risky choices across subjects (a within-task, task-related contrast) — meeting I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses with coordinates for hippocampus and putamen), satisfying I6 and acceptable under I7. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes full methods, results, and discussion, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Although the study conducted an fMRI during a decision-making (probabilistic reversal learning) task and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts of model-derived reward prediction errors, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. This paper examines monetary reward prediction errors and ADHD-related learning/decision mechanisms rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward images. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to decision-making: RPEcue and RPEoutcome), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (results reported in tables/figures/text). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6. Primary reason for exclusion: study does not address the review’s topical objective (reward cue-reactivity to drug/natural stimuli).

The study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a modified Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task), satisfying I4. It includes model-based, trial-to-trial prediction error analyses and reports task-related contrasts (prediction error tracking) and behavioral correlations, satisfying I5. The paper conducts and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (two-sample t tests and cluster-corrected maps) for the prediction-error regressor and provides clusters/tables/figures, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply: the study reports whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), and provides primary task effects rather than only between-group interactions without unmasked whole-brain effects. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The full text is complete and reports whole-brain fMRI task activation maps during a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) task. However, it does not meet the review’s task-based inclusion criteria: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task but a probabilistic reversal learning/reinforcement-learning task) and I5 (contrasts reported are reward-sensitivity and cognitive-flexibility contrasts, not risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts such as "risky > safe" or "ambiguous > non-ambiguous"). It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Therefore the study is excluded because key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied.

While this is an empirical fMRI study of human perceptual decision-making (categorization) and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results using searchlight MVPA, it does not address the meta-analysis topic of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper investigates category learning and perceptual choices (radial vs. concentric Glass patterns) rather than cue-reactivity to reward-related stimuli; therefore it is not relevant to the review objective and should be excluded.

Although this paper reports a human fMRI experiment with risky and ambiguous decision-making and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > risk; risk > ambiguity) with coordinates and statistics, it does NOT address the stated meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts: ambiguous>non-ambiguous; risk>ambiguity), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met relative to meta-analysis objective: the study does not investigate cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual cues, so it does not address the review topic and should be excluded on that basis.

This study meets the review's decision-making fMRI inclusion criteria: (I4) participants performed an fMRI Risky Gains Task (risky decision-making), (I5) it reports within-task contrasts comparing risky vs safe decisions (risky–safe) and group-by-decision effects, (I6) voxelwise group-level analyses were performed and whole-brain group-by-decision results are reported (supplementary whole-brain analysis and coordinates), and (I7) coordinates/figures/tables are provided for significant clusters. It does not violate exclusion criteria: it is not ROI-only (whole-brain results are reported), not a connectivity/resting-only study, not non-empirical, and includes task-evoked activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present); supplementary materials are referenced but their absence does not preclude inclusion. Therefore include.

This study employed fMRI during a monetary two-choice decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports a within-task contrast of risky > safe selections (Select 10/30 > 70/90), so it meets I4 and I5. However, the primary neuroimaging analyses were restricted to a priori small-volume ROIs (OFC/VLPFC and ACC) with small-volume correction and ROI-based peak reporting; the manuscript does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required by I6. Thus the study reports only ROI-based results and falls under exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Therefore the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing an adapted Iowa Gambling Task, which is a risky/ambiguous decision-making task (meets I4). It includes within-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous decision-making (e.g., disadvantageous > advantageous choices; win > loss; EV-modulated win/loss contrasts) (meets I5). Analyses are group-level whole-brain, voxelwise maps using permutation-based cluster analysis and report coordinates and cluster tables (meets I6 and I7). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, and is empirical original fMRI data). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. Although it is an empirical fMRI study of risky decision-making and provides group-level, whole-brain statistical maps, its task investigates gain/loss framing and cognitive engagement—not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to decision-making; frame-consistent vs frame-inconsistent and choice regressors), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps; unthresholded map available), I7 (whole-brain results clearly described and maps deposited). Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E6 apply. Because the review requires studies specifically about drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, this study is out of scope and must be excluded.

This is a human fMRI study using a perceptual decision-making task (orientation discrimination of Gabor patches) with visual reward-predictive cues and natural reward (juice). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses correlating trial-by-trial model regressors (predicted reward V(t) and reward prediction error δ(t)) with BOLD signals, including FDR-corrected maps and peak MNI coordinates. The study manipulates stimulus discriminability (high vs low contrast) and examines its effect on brain responses, satisfying perceptual-decision contrasts related to stimulus difficulty/discriminability. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric effects tied to perceptual discriminability), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (coordinates and figures reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported) and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task—the High/Low Card Guessing Task is a reward-processing task without explicit risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty), and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making are provided). The study also does not address drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (meta-analysis objective). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making task (probability discounting) during scanning, with within-task parametric contrasts related to risk (subjective value of the risky option, chosen value, decision conflict) and categorical task effects. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM8), with statistical maps, tables of coordinates (Table 1), and figures showing voxelwise results; ROI/SVC analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are present. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making paradigm (Colorado Balloon Game), fulfilling I4. It includes within-task contrasts isolating decision-related activity (Decision Trial – Directed Trial) and separates deliberations preceding risky vs. cautious responses, fulfilling I5. Analyses are reported as group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM8 analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and Monte Carlo estimation; results are described in tables/figures, satisfying I6 and I7. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state, and presents whole-brain task activation contrasts (not only between-group contrasts without task effects), so no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article should be included for the meta-analysis.

Full text reports an fMRI study in healthy humans performing a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty) and includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with reported coordinates. However, it does not report any within-task or between-task contrasts that map onto the review’s required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”). The reported regressors are model-based signals (prior correct/prior incorrect, posterior–prior update, switch>stay) rather than contrasts of risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty per the meta-analysis inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study includes fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task and reports whole-brain group-level activation contrasts (satisfying I4, I5, I6, and I7), it does not address the meta-analysis topic of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The experimental paradigm analyses face gender categorization and the effects of visual noise—there are no reward-related cues, drug stimuli, or reward-cue reactivity contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is not relevant to the review objective and must be excluded for topic/domain mismatch.

Although this study is an fMRI investigation in healthy adults and meets the methodological inclusion criteria for decision-making tasks (I4, I5) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (I6, I7), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paradigm is a probabilistic reasoning/uncertainty (beads/JTC) task rather than a cue-reactivity task involving drug or natural reward cues. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met relative to the review objective: the study does not investigate reward-related cue-reactivity (topic mismatch). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of probabilistic category learning (weather prediction task) in women with subthreshold bulimia versus controls. It does not investigate drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and does not employ a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrast as specified. Critically, analyses were performed using an ROI-based SPM factorial ANOVA (AAL masks) rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map. Therefore Exclusion E3 applies (only ROI analyses reported with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria I4–I7 are not met: I4 (risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) — NOT met; I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision-making) — NOT met; I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map) — NOT met; I7 (whole-brain results acceptable in tables/figures/text) — NOT met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although the study does include an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (auditory/vocal emotions) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses and contrasts, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (perceptual decision-making fMRI), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported with peak coordinates/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6. Primary reason for exclusion: study population/task/stimuli do not involve reward-related cue-reactivity nor visual stimuli required by the review objective, so it is not relevant to the review.

Although the study includes an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed an ambiguous perceptual/valence decision (intermediate dissonance > consonance) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinates/figures (I4, I5, I6, I7 are satisfied), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. This study uses auditory (musical) stimuli and investigates emotional valence and uncertainty, not reward-related cue reactivity or visual cue processing. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are met. Therefore it must be excluded because it does not match the review topic (reward-related, visual cue-reactivity).

This study meets all specified inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies. I4: Subjects underwent fMRI while performing a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game). I5: The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (DecBa vs DirBa; decision-period contrasts; win vs loss contrasts). I6: Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed (SPM5 ANCOVA; cluster-level FWE/AlphaSim corrections). I7: Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures with coordinates and detailed description in text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not only between-group contrasts without unmasked task effects; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI case–control study in humans using a risky economic decision-making task (mixed gambles) during scanning, with trial-by-trial parametric modulators for gains and losses and group-level second-level analyses. The paper reports voxelwise task-evoked results (including whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables/figures and ROI-corrected voxelwise results) and contrasts related to valuation/risk (neural gain–loss coding, loss coding, group interactions). Thus it meets the required criteria for task type, within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making, and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise reporting (coordinates/tables). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The study is an fMRI empirical study of navigation under uncertainty and meets the decision-making inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous/partially observable decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast: goal-search > visuomotor control and parametric regressors of uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), and I7 (results reported with coordinates and ROI analyses). However, it does NOT address the meta-analysis topic of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (topic/domain mismatch). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded due to failure to address the review objective (reward-related cue-reactivity).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (n=6) that implemented perceptual decision-making tasks (difference judgments across visual and auditory modalities) during scanning. The authors report within-task contrasts comparing judgment > passive viewing/blank and present group-level mixed-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL) with cluster-thresholded activation maps and Talairach coordinates/figures. Thus it satisfies I4 (perceptual decision-making task during fMRI), I5 (perceptual-task > control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported as figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This single-case fMRI study does not address the review objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli). Although it contains task-based fMRI during decision-making and reports contrasts, it is a single-subject/case study rather than a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts, e.g., A>B), and I7 (coordinates reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map). No exclusion criteria E3–E5 apply directly, but failure to meet I6 and mismatch with the review objective require exclusion.

This study conducted whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI analyses and reports cluster-level, FWE-corrected task activation maps (meets I6) and reports whole-brain results described in text/figures/tables (meets I7). However, it does not test a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast of the type required: the task is a reversal-learning reward/punishment paradigm and reported contrasts are reward vs punishment (punished correct vs rewarded correct) and group comparisons; these are reward outcome/valence contrasts rather than explicit risky/ambiguity/perceptual decision-making contrasts (I4 and I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I4 and I5.

This study reports an fMRI delay-discounting decision-making task (hard, easy, no trials) in HIV-positive adults with contrasts including hard>easy, hard>no, and easy>no. The methods describe group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and results presented in tables and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The task is a perceptual/decision-making paradigm (delay discounting) and includes the required within-task contrasts (hard>easy). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for decision-making perceptual contrasts and whole-brain group-level activation reporting.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion). The analysis includes within-task contrasts comparing coherence levels (low coherence > high coherence), matching the perceptual-DM contrast examples in I5. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and group maps with permutation testing and cluster correction (satisfying I6/I7). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study of visual natural (sexual) cues and reports group-level voxelwise task activation maps, it does NOT meet the meta-analysis' task-related inclusion requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported) and I7 (results are clearly described in text and figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (the experiment is a response-inhibition erotic Go/NoGo task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as specified) and I5 (the reported contrasts are NoGo>Go, Male>Female, and related interaction contrasts—not contrasts framed as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy perceptual decisions). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failure to meet I4 and I5.

Although this paper meets the methodological inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies (see below), it does not address the review objective of reward-related cue-reactivity to visual drug or natural reward cues. The study investigates pain perception and threat manipulation using laser stimuli (somatosensory, not visual reward cues). Therefore it is not relevant to a meta-analysis of reward cue-reactivity and is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast: pain > no pain / pain vs no-pain decisions), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses), I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 are unmet, but the study does not address the overarching review topic (reward-related visual cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a decision-making task (a modified ultimatum game) in which proposers choose between fair and selfish offers that carry varying risk of rejection. The contrasts reported (e.g., choosing slightly selfish > fair; fair > selfish; high stakes > low stakes) are within-task decision-making contrasts reflecting choices under risk/uncertainty. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM with reported cluster-level results and MNI coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (task-based fMRI of risky/decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (results reported with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of decision-making on abstract value word pairs in managers vs. non-managers, not a drug or natural reward cue-reactivity study using visual reward cues. It does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as required (I4 and I5 not met). The paper does report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results and lists coordinates (so I6 and I7 are satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study should be excluded because it does not address the review objective and fails to meet I4 and I5.

Although this fMRI study used a risky decision-making task (Social Analogue Risk Task) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (parametric modulation during cash-out decisions) with coordinates and cluster-corrected maps, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. The stimuli are dynamically changing facial expressions (social cues), not drug or natural reward cues, so the paper is not relevant to the review question. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (risky decision-making fMRI task), I5 (within-task contrast / parametric modulation related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 are unmet. Exclusion criteria met: none. Final decision: EXCLUDED due to lack of relevance to reward cue-reactivity (study does not examine drug/natural reward visual cues).

This study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the review. Matched to inclusion criteria: I4: Yes — fMRI was conducted while adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). I6: Yes — group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (Win vs No Win) are reported and cluster-corrected. I7: Yes — whole-brain results are clearly described and displayed. Not met: I5 — the reported contrasts focus on reward feedback (Win vs No Win) rather than a contrast directly related to risky vs safe decision-making (e.g., risky>safe); no risky>safe (or equivalent risk-related) contrast is reported in the results. Additionally, the study does not address the stated meta-analysis objective of drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (cue-reactivity of drug/natural rewards), so it is not conceptually aligned with the review objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered.

This human fMRI study scanned participants performing a decision-making/reinforcement-learning task involving uncertainty-driven exploration (stop-the-clock RT task). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts related to uncertainty (relative and mean uncertainty) and tests effects in explorers vs. non-explorers. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected results reported. The full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the specified inclusion criteria for task type, relevant contrasts, and whole-brain reporting (I4–I7). No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is complete. This fMRI study reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps (I6) and presents whole-brain results in text/tables (I7). However, it does not test a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as required (I4 not satisfied) and does not provide within-task contrasts that map onto the meta-analysis examples (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy)—the reported contrasts focus on error/negative-feedback (reversal switch errors vs correct responses, nonswitch errors vs correct responses) and treatment×task interactions rather than risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrasts (I5 not satisfied). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore exclude because inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met; inclusion criteria met: I6, I7; exclusion criteria met: none.

The full text is complete and the study is an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in humans. It meets the listed inclusion criteria for decision-making studies: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts such as high-risk > low-risk and risky > safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I7 (results reported as peak coordinates/tables). However, it does NOT address the review objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (i.e., it examines risky decision-making rather than cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not match the meta-analysis review objective (reward cue-reactivity). Full text is complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment of social cooperation (trust/reciprocity games), not drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, so it does not address the stated review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — trust game involves risky choices) and I6/I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported and whole-brain results described/figures provided). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the paper does not report a within-task or between-task contrast explicitly related to risky vs safe (e.g., risky > safe) or other risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts; the primary reported contrasts compare human versus computer counterparts and cooperators versus noncooperators. Additionally, the content does not involve drug/natural reward cue-reactivity or visual cue presentations relevant to the review objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the methods/results reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given the mismatch with the review objective and absence of the required risk-related contrast (I5), exclude.

This study does not meet the review’s task-type inclusion requirements. Although it is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study with group-level voxelwise analyses reported (I6) and whole-brain results described in the text/tables (I7), it used a probabilistic reversal-learning reward task and contrasts such as negative > positive feedback, final reversal > reversal error, and final reversal error > correct responses. These contrasts do not correspond to the risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts specified by the inclusion criteria (I4 and I5), nor does the study examine cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual cues targeted by the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded because I4 and I5 are not satisfied.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (estimating a briefly flashed stimulus location) and includes within-task contrasts comparing conditions (e.g., individual information alone vs integration conditions I:I, I:S, S:S). Imaging was analyzed at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM8 analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and reported peak MNI coordinates. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked activation maps relevant to perceptual decision-making. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune), satisfying I4. The authors present within-task contrasts directly related to risk (Risk vs. No-Risk; comparisons of probabilistic vs. sure trials), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted using FLAME and cluster-corrected voxelwise thresholds, with results reported in figures and tables, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete=false is not set). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria and is INCLUDED in the review.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none (no E3–E6 violations). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/uncertain decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast: uncertain > certain), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: Although the study satisfies the decision-making-related inclusion criteria above, it does NOT address the review’s primary objective (meta-analysis of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). The paper investigates risky decision making in internet gaming disorder rather than visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards; therefore it is not relevant to the stated review objective and should be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study with group-level and whole-brain analyses (meets I6 and I7). However, the task is a probabilistic classification/feedback learning task (informational feedback), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore it does not satisfy I4 (task type) nor I5 (within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Summary: Inclusion met: I6, I7. Inclusion not met: I4, I5. Exclusion met: none (E3–E6: none). Consequently the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) inside a 3T scanner with within-task contrasts (bias cue vs neutral cue and stimulus-level valid/invalid contrasts). The authors conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FEAT, FLAME) and report cluster-corrected and uncorrected whole-brain results/figures. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I7 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies. It reports an fMRI scan in human participants performing a validated risky decision-making task (modified Lane risk-taking task) (I4). The paper includes within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., risky > safe; win > safe; loss > safe) and condition contrasts (alcohol vs placebo) (I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps (AFNI 3dANOVA/3dttest) with cluster-correction and coordinates reported in tables/figures (I6, I7). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without task effect, and an empirical study with original fMRI data). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although this paper used fMRI in humans performing a risky lottery decision-making task (I4) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with reported coordinates and multiple-comparison correction (satisfying I6 and I7), it does not present a within-task or between-task contrast that isolates risk level (e.g., "risky > safe", "high-risk > low-risk", "riskier > surer"). The reported neuroimaging contrasts focus on social vs. private contexts and outcome valence (social gain/loss) rather than explicit risk-level contrasts. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game) in the scanner, satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts directly contrasting risky versus safe decisions (e.g., Go > Stop) and outcome contrasts (Good > Bad), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (whole-brain tables/figures, cluster correction via 3dClustSim) and NeuroVault maps are provided, satisfying I6 and I7. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making whole-brain task activation and is INCLUDED.

The study reports fMRI during a delay-discounting (intertemporal choice) task in adolescent substance users with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (SS vs CON; LL vs CON) and ICA results. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps are reported) and I7 (results reported in tables/figures/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is intertemporal delay discounting, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as specified) and I5 (no contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making, e.g., “risky > safe” or “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the required task-domain inclusion criteria (I4 and I5).

This study used fMRI during the Iowa Gambling Task, a risky decision-making paradigm, and reports contrasts comparing high-risk versus low-risk choices. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3×2×3 ANOVA) are reported, with results presented in tables and figures; cluster-level correction (AlphaSim SVC) was applied. Thus it satisfies I4 (task type), I5 (risk-related contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E5) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an event-related fMRI reversal learning task in euthymic pediatric bipolar disorder versus controls. While it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain corrected ANOVA reported and results presented in text/tables), it does not examine drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli nor does it implement a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as required by the review. Therefore it fails the key content-related inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choice between risky £1 vs safer 10p options) during fMRI under ketamine and placebo. The paper reports within-task computationally derived contrasts related to risk-related decision variables (choice temperature, learning rate; outcome confirmatory vs contradictory), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample and paired t-tests) and reports results in text/figures/ROIs. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/decision variables), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Although it reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (I6) and presents whole-brain results in tables/figures (I7), it does not implement a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (I4 not met). It also does not report the required within-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria applied: none.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a card gambling task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk (decision-phase regressors for six risk levels; outcome contrasts grouped by risk level; risk magnitude linear effects) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and stereotactic coordinates reported. Results and contrasts relevant to risk (e.g., risk level effects, low-risk vs high-risk negative outcomes, risk-related linear increase in VS) are described in the text and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and is empirical).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it reports a human fMRI experiment in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination) (I4). The paper includes within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., Fin vs Nin, Hin vs Nin, In vs Out, task-onset contrasts; analogous to “perceptual task > control” and low/high coherence contrasts) (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects second-level analyses, whole-brain contrasts with cluster/FWE corrections) and whole-brain results are presented in figures/text (I6, I7). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Although this fMRI study uses a risky, value-based lottery decision task and reports whole-brain, group-level, task-evoked maps (satisfying I4, I5, I6, I7), it does not address the meta-analysis objective: drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. The task involves monetary lotteries and Bayesian integration of prior and likelihood information rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclude on the basis of not addressing the review’s topical scope (cue-reactivity).

The study used fMRI and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (I6 satisfied) and presents results in text/figures (I7 satisfied). However, it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task: participants passively viewed stimulus sequences and provided post-hoc causal ratings rather than making in-task risky/ambiguous/perceptual choices, and no within-task contrasts of the form 'risky > safe', 'ambiguity > non-ambiguity', or 'hard > easy' are reported. Therefore it fails I4 and I5 and does not meet the review’s task-specific inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house discrimination) with within-task contrasts (e.g., HF > FH, FFhc > HHhc) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected clusters reported for HF > FH). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling verification of whole-brain task-evoked maps. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli: this paper investigates decoding of near-threshold pain perception using laser somatosensory stimulation and multivariate analyses, not reward cue-reactivity or visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (perceptual decision-making task: subjects judged painful vs non-painful), I5 (within-task contrasts/decoding for perceptual decisions such as pain vs no-pain/anticipation vs stimulation), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses and voxelwise maps reported), I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (none of I4–I7 are unmet). Exclusion criteria met: [] (none of E3–E6 apply). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (core article content present: Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study used fMRI of probabilistic association learning (Weather Prediction Task) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy), nor does it address reward-related cue-reactivity with visual stimuli which is the meta-analysis objective. Therefore it fails to meet I4 and I5 despite providing whole-brain results. Full text appears complete.

Although this paper is an fMRI study of risky decision-making that reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and task contrasts, it does not address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (risky decision-making fMRI task), I5 (within-task/between-task contrasts related to risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported with coordinates/parametric maps). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I4–I7 are unmet. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Primary reason for exclusion: topic mismatch — the study investigates monetary risky choices and conflict monitoring, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual stimuli, so it does not address the review objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which human participants (pathological gamblers and matched controls) performed the Iowa Gambling Task during scanning (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task and between-task contrasts related to risk (high-risk vs low-risk deck selections) and presents group-level mixed-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholded maps and cluster-correction, with activation clusters/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Although it is an empirical fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain task activation maps (satisfying I6 and I7), it does not employ a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (violates I4) and does not report any within-task contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”), violating I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a validated risk-taking decision-making task, and a go/no-go cognitive control task. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (FSL FLAME; cluster-forming threshold Z>2.3, p<.05 FWE corrected) and provides tables/coordinates and figures. Relevant contrasts include Pumps > Control (color pumps vs. white control pumps), Cash Outs > Baseline, and Explosions > Baseline, satisfying a within-task risk-related contrast. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts without an unmasked whole-brain task effect, and is an empirical fMRI study with original data. The provided full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy humans performing an ambiguous decision-making task (certain vs uncertain rule). It reports within-task contrasts (uncertain > certain and certain > uncertain) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (FEAT; cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with figures and text describing activations. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses a probabilistic reversal-learning task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses with coordinates. However, it does not examine risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined by the inclusion criteria (e.g., no contrasts such as risky > safe, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, or hard > easy). The reported contrasts focus on feedback and reversal-related events (e.g., FINREVERR vs REVERR, ALLNEG vs ALLPOS, NEG+2 vs NEG+0), which do not map onto the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts required (I5). Therefore, although I6 and I7 are satisfied (whole-brain group maps reported), the key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a sequential risky decision-making task with parametric analyses of risk (variance), expected value, and skewness. Group-level, whole-brain SPM random-effects analyses are reported with thresholded maps and stereotactic coordinates; results are presented in figures/tables and supplemental material. Thus the report satisfies the required elements: (I4) fMRI during a risky decision-making task; (I5) within-task contrasts/parametric effects related to risk/variance and value; (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses; (I7) results reported via coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not meet the review’s task domain criteria. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported and voxel-wise t-tests with cluster correction are described) and I7 (whole-brain results are reported in text/figures). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (the fMRI task is the Monetary Incentive Delay task, which measures reward anticipation/receipt and simple reaction-time responding, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making such as “risky>safe”, “ambiguity>non-ambiguity”, or “hard>easy” are reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED.
