Although the full text is complete and the fMRI methods match the decision-making criteria (I4-I7 are satisfied: an fMRI was acquired during a risky decision-making task—the Iowa Gambling Task—contrasts comparing bad>good choices are reported, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and FWE correction are provided), the study does NOT address the stated meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. This paper investigates persuasive messaging effects on risk appraisal and choice behavior during the IGT, not visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Therefore it is not topical for the meta-analysis and is excluded on that basis. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI Risky Gains Task (a risky decision-making task) with explicit within-task contrasts (risky > safe decisions; risky wins > losses) and conducts whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with tables/figures of significant clusters. The full text includes introduction, methods (task, imaging, preprocessing, voxelwise analyses), results (decision and outcome contrasts, voxelwise cluster results), and discussion, allowing verification of whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes whole-brain task effects rather than only between-group effects). Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria for decision-making fMRI studies and is suitable for inclusion.

This study used task-based fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a canonical risky decision-making task), includes within-task contrasts (parametric modulation of pump number and mean pump vs control-balloon contrasts), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain cluster-corrected results reported and coordinates provided). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core article content is present. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and provides whole-brain task effects).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (object recognition under masked revelation). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to recognition time, accuracy, and trial type (e.g., comparisons across TRs, correct vs TR8, static vs shuffle) and tests effects on BOLD slope/onset. Analyses were voxelwise, group-level, whole-brain GLM maps (main effect of time images, thresholded and corrected) used to define ROIs and reported in figures/tables. Thus the study meets I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (card prediction task: uncertain vs certain trials). It includes an explicit within-task contrast (Uncertain > Certain) and reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain analyses with corrected cluster results and Talairach coordinates (Table 2), fulfilling whole-brain reporting standards. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic/ambiguous decision-making (categorization) task. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to rate/strength of evidence (e.g., Rapid>Gradual>Switch and Switch>Gradual>Rapid) and analyses of evidence x time interactions. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM/ANOVA maps with corrected cluster-wise inference and peak coordinates reported in tables/figures. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the listed inclusion criteria for task type, within-task contrasts, whole-brain group maps, and reporting format.

This is an fMRI study using a probabilistic reversal learning task in adolescents with detailed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (coordinates/clusters reported) and task contrasts (punished reversal errors vs rewarded correct responses). However, the meta-analysis requires studies of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making with at least one contrast explicitly reflecting risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, “hard > easy”). This study’s task and reported contrasts index reversal learning/prediction-error and reinforcement processing rather than the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts. Therefore I4 and I5 are not satisfied despite meeting whole-brain reporting requirements (I6, I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of perceptual decision-making (dot-motion coherence) with whole-brain, group-level analyses and reported task contrasts; it therefore meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. However, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (no reward or cue-reactivity paradigm, no substance/natural reward stimuli or related contrasts). None of the exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply (the study reports whole-brain results, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, includes within-subject task effects, and is empirical). Because the study does not address the review topic (reward cue-reactivity), it must be excluded.

Although this study meets the technical fMRI decision-making criteria (I4–I7), it does NOT address the meta-analysis review objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. Specifically: inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task — Iowa Gambling Task), I5 (within-task contrast: decision-making > control), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (results reported in figures/tables/text). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Inclusion criteria not met relative to the review objective: the study does not examine cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual cues (the primary review topic), so it is ineligible for this reward-cue meta-analysis despite meeting I4–I7. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion categorization varying motion coherence) and reports within-task contrasts and parametric analyses directly related to perceptual difficulty (e.g., motion coherence low>high, parametric coherence effects). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (cluster-corrected maps, MNI normalization) with results presented in figures and tables of coordinates. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (perceptual contrasts such as low vs. high coherence and parametric tests), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI gambling task probing risky decision-making in healthy high- and low-risk twins. It includes an explicit risky > safe / risk-magnitude contrast (a linear gambling risk contrast across 6 risk levels) during the choice phase (meets I5). Data were acquired with task-evoked, group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM8 and report cluster-level results with FWE correction and stereotactic coordinates (meets I6 and I7). The experiment is a task-based fMRI during risky decision making (meets I4). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study fits the review’s risky-DM inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study does not address the review objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Although it is an empirical human fMRI study with perceptual decision-making tasks (spatial and shape comparisons) and reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (e.g., task > baseline; hard/easy comparisons), satisfying I4, I5, I6 and I7, its content focuses on spatial encoding/scene-selective cortex and resting-state connectivity rather than reward-cue reactivity. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Excluded for lack of topical relevance to the meta-analysis objective.

Although this full text contains an fMRI risky decision-making task with appropriate within-task contrasts and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates/tables/figures), it does NOT address the stated meta-analysis objective (fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). The study investigates personality-related differences in risky decision-making (Risky-Gains Task) rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues presented visually; therefore it is not topical for the review. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an event-related whole-brain fMRI investigation of sequential predictability (SRTT) and hippocampal responses to mutual information. While it reports group-level whole-brain results with coordinates (satisfying I6 and I7), it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (I4 not met). It also does not report any within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty (e.g., “hard>easy”, “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”) required by I5. Therefore it does not meet the core task-related inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study does not address the review objective (fMRI of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Although it is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study of perceptual decision making and includes contrasts relating to perceptual difficulty/coherence, it investigates face/car perceptual discrimination and EEG-informed component regressors rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Exclusion IDs met: none of E3–E6 apply. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual difficulty/low vs high coherence), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (results reported in text/figures/tables). Inclusion IDs not met: the study does NOT examine drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and therefore does not address the review objective. Full text appears complete.

Although the study involves perceptual decision-making tasks performed in MRI sessions (Experiments 1–3 include MRI/mock-MRI sessions), the full text presents behavioral analyses and LBA modeling only and does not report any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked fMRI activation maps or task contrasts (e.g., hard>easy) required for inclusion. Therefore: inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI session with perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported within- or between-task fMRI contrasts in this paper), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly triggered by the content provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it lacks the required whole-brain fMRI activation/contrast data.

Although this paper reports empirical fMRI data with a risky/uncertain decision-making task and whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (meets I4, I5, I6, I7), it does not address the meta-analysis objective: drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual reward cues. The study investigates probability learning and decision-making for monetary payoffs rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Therefore it is not relevant to the review's topic and is excluded on that basis. Full text is complete.

Although this paper meets the technical fMRI inclusion criteria (see below), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Specifically, this is an fMRI study of attentional deployment and regret in a sequential risk-taking task with monetary/gold outcomes, not a cue-reactivity study of drug or natural rewards. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk: Opt vs Nopt, GF vs MF, etc.), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. Because the study does not address the review objective (drug/natural reward cue-reactivity), it is excluded.

Although this fMRI study used perceptual/ambiguous target-detection and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (meeting I4–I7), it does not address the review’s topical objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The task involves visual target/distractor morphs and attentional/ambiguity contrasts rather than reward-cue reactivity or drug/natural reward stimuli. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Therefore the study is ineligible for this reward cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

The study does not address the review objective (fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Although it is an empirical fMRI study of perceptual decision-making with group-level, whole-brain searchlight maps, it uses auditory and tactile stimuli and investigates category representations via MVPA rather than reward cue-reactivity to visual cues. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps from searchlight/t-statistics), I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no within-task or between-task univariate contrasts of the form required for perceptual decision-making meta-analyses such as “hard > easy” or “perceptual task > control”), and the study does not involve drug/natural reward cue-reactivity or visual stimuli as required by the review objective. Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI but during a working-memory (n-back) task, not while participants performed a risky/ambiguous decision-making task (IGT). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the 2-back>0-back contrast) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrast related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making was reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a decision-making task under uncertainty (matching-pennies). The paper reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses and task contrasts relevant to ambiguity/uncertainty and decision-making (e.g., uncertain > certain; feedback > no-feedback; high-load > low-load), with coordinates and ROI tables (whole-brain results reported). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies the inclusion criteria for an fMRI study of uncertain/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (I4, I5) and provides whole-brain group-level activation maps/coordinates (I6, I7). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an event-related, whole-brain fMRI study of human decision-making (Iowa Gambling Task) and meets the methodological fMRI inclusion criteria, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Specifically: the task involves monetary decision-making under uncertainty (IGT), not cue-reactivity paradigms featuring drug or natural reward cues (visual). Therefore it is not relevant to the review question and must be excluded. The paper does perform whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reports task contrasts (anticipation vs experience; gain/draw/loss; deck contrasts), but the population and task are outside the scope of reward cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply.

Exclusion rationale: Although the full text is complete and the study meets the methodological inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7: it is an fMRI study with a risky decision-making task, reports within-task contrasts such as Play>Pass and HR>LR, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinates), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. Therefore it is not relevant to the review question and is excluded. Exclusion IDs met: none of E3–E6. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: the study does not address the review’s topical requirement (visual cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that used a perceptual decision-making (time-pressured Go/No-Go “READ-M” baseball) task and reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses. It meets inclusion criteria: I4 — subjects performed a perceptual decision-making task (Go/No-Go perceptual judgments); I5 — the authors report within-task contrasts/analyses (behaviorally Correct vs Incorrect trials, Correct Go vs Correct No-Go, etc.) used in searchlight/GLM comparisons; I6 — group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (GLM PEs, searchlight AUC maps and permutation-derived p-value maps in MNI space); I7 — whole-brain results are reported in figures and supplementary tables (node coordinates and statistical maps described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary references). Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a reward-based decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune), with explicit risky vs. safe contrasts reported. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps and reports coordinates and figures for task effects and between-group comparisons (risk>safe and related contrasts). Thus it meets I4 (task is risky decision-making), I5 (risky>safe contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), and I7 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), include whole-brain task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), and it is an empirical study with original fMRI data (not excluded by E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article reports an fMRI study in human adolescents performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task), with within-task contrasts explicitly comparing risky versus non-risky decisions (Mean Color > Mean White; Linear Color > Linear White). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL/FLAME and results are reported as cluster-corrected maps and tables (figures/tables and supplementary figures describing whole-brain effects are provided). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplemental materials) is available. Therefore it satisfies I4 (task-based fMRI of risky decision-making), I5 (within-task risky>safe contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing risky and intertemporal decision-making tasks using visual monetary gambles. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk and delay (e.g., Risk > Control, Risk > Delay, Delay > Control, Delay > Risk) and choice-prediction contrasts. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables/figures providing coordinates. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study acquired task-based fMRI during a gambling decision-making task with explicit high-uncertainty (Lose) vs low-uncertainty (Win) conditions, providing within-task contrasts (Lose vs Win). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses were conducted with SPM8 (reported task condition main effects and coordinates/tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Results and contrasts relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity/resting-state, and is empirical). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete.

This study does not address the review objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli and does not report contrasts explicitly targeted to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported with whole-brain FWE results) and I7 (whole-brain results are reported and described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the fMRI task is a reward-guided probabilistic reversal/exploration-exploitation decision task rather than an explicitly risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review) and I5 (no within-task contrasts framed as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or perceptual difficulty contrasts; reported contrasts focus on model-based prediction errors and exploratory vs exploitative trials). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual two-alternative forced-choice task (face vs house) manipulating stimulus difficulty (phase coherence). It includes within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., hard > easy; low coherence > high coherence) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-corrected) with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Results and contrasts are described in the text and tables/figures. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical fMRI in healthy adults). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

Although this paper meets the technical fMRI inclusion criteria (I4–I7: it used an fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making task (IGT), reports within-task contrasts (e.g., risky > safe, anticipation, win > loss), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported in text/tables/figures), it does not address the review objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. This study examines monetary reward-based decision-making and neural responses during the IGT rather than visual cue-reactivity to drugs/natural rewards. Therefore it is excluded for not matching the review’s topical objective. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study with whole-brain task maps and within-task contrasts of decision-making under uncertainty, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective. The paper reports a 4-arm bandit decision-making task probing exploration/exploitation and model-based uncertainty, not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual cues. Therefore it is not relevant to a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug/natural reward visual stimuli and must be excluded.

Although this study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI results during a reward-guided decision-making (probabilistic reversal) task and provides voxelwise maps (meets I4, I6, I7), it does not report any within-task or between-task contrasts explicitly targeting risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). Reported contrasts focus on reward vs. punishment and model-derived prediction-error parametric effects, not on risk/ambiguity or perceptual difficulty contrasts required by I5. Therefore I5 is not met and the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that implemented a risky decision-making (roulette) task contrasting low- vs high-probability (risky vs safe) and gain vs loss conditions. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., high vs low probability, gain > loss) and group-level analyses. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results are described (whole-brain analyses and Supplementary Tables of activated foci are referenced), in addition to ROI analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Stoplight) during scanning and includes within-task contrasts (e.g., Go > Stop, Stop > Go, Crash > NoCrash) including comparisons pre- vs post-exclusion. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted and results are reported with coordinate tables and figures. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI results of a risky decision-making task (BART) and provides relevant contrasts, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. Specifically: (a) Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk: parametric active pumps vs control, active vs control, cash-out, explosion), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported and thresholded), I7 (results reported in text/tables/figures). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: The study is not a cue-reactivity paradigm involving drug or natural reward visual cues and therefore does not address the review’s topical objective. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of risky monetary decision-making strategies (Pmax/Gmax/Lmin) using multi-outcome gambles. It meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing risky/strategy choices), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with cluster correction), and I7 (coordinates and whole-brain results provided). However, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli: there are no drug/natural reward cues or cue-reactivity contrasts reported (the outcomes are monetary gambles resolved after decisions). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore I exclude the study because it fails to meet the overarching review objective (cue-reactivity to visual drug/natural rewards).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans that used a perceptual decision-making task (near-threshold Gabor detection) during scanning, meeting I4. The authors report within-task contrasts related to perceptual decisions (e.g., expectation-incongruent > expectation-congruent, unexpected > expected stimulus), meeting I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (with peak thresholds, cluster-level FDR/FWE corrections, and whole-brain cluster tables/coordinates), satisfying I6 and I7. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods (participants, design, staircases, MRI acquisition, GLM), Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of perceptual cue-related decision-making with visual stimuli.

The study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a decision-making task—probabilistic reversal learning), I6 (group-level voxelwise discriminability maps / random-effects voxelwise results are reported; Fig. 2B), and I7 (whole-brain results are presented in figures and described). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the paper does not present within-task or between-task contrasts corresponding to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Instead the primary analyses focus on decoding “switch vs. stay” decisions and region-based multivariate classifiers, which do not map onto the required risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper should be excluded.

The full text is complete. While this fMRI study reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation and provides coordinate tables (meets I6 and I7), it does NOT meet the critical task-based inclusion criteria. The task is a probabilistic feedback expectancy/reward task without participant choices between risky vs safe or ambiguous vs unambiguous options; participants did not perform a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (fails I4). Consequently, no within-task contrasts of the types required for decision-making meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) are reported (fails I5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I4 and I5, despite providing whole-brain results (I6, I7).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing an intertemporal decision-making task that manipulates time-ambiguity (ambiguous vs exact delays). It includes within-task contrasts directly relevant to ambiguity (Ambiguous > Exact; SV Amb vs SV Ex), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM12, cluster FWE-corrected results). Whole-brain results are presented in the text and supplemental materials. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The paper reports simultaneous EEG-fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning reward-learning task and provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and coordinate tables (meets I6 and I7). However, the task is a reward-learning paradigm rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as specified in I4, and the reported contrasts focus on outcome valence and unsigned prediction error (surprise) rather than contrasts explicitly comparing risk/ambiguity or perceptual difficulty conditions required by I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Thus the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5 are not met) and is excluded.

Excluded because the study does not provide whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and reports results primarily using ROI-constrained analyses (Exclusion E3). It does include an fMRI task involving probabilistic reversal learning (meets I4: task-based fMRI) and includes within-task contrasts related to adaptive behaviour after feedback (meets I5). However, it does NOT meet I6 (no unmasked whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported; results were SVC within pre-specified ROIs) and I7 (no acceptable whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Additionally, the study topic (probabilistic reversal learning in anorexia nervosa) does not address the review objective of cue-reactivity to drug/natural reward visual stimuli. Full text appears complete.

The study reports fMRI in human participants performing a mixed gambles risky decision-making task (50/50 gain/loss), includes within-task contrasts (Accepted>Baseline, Rejected>Baseline, Accepted>Rejected), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4–I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study meets the decision-making fMRI inclusion criteria: participants performed the Decision-Reward Uncertainty Task (risky/uncertain decision-making) during fMRI (I4). Relevant task contrasts are reported (behavioral risk > reward risk/no-risk; reward > no-reward), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with reported clusters and coordinates (thresholded maps, Tables/Figures), meeting I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the article should be INCLUDED.

While the study meets the methodological inclusion criteria for this review (I4–I7: it used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task, reported within-task contrasts, and produced group-level voxelwise maps with reported coordinates), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective: drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study investigates threat-related (fear) cueing and emotional face perception rather than reward cue-reactivity (drug or natural rewards). Therefore it is not relevant to the review objective and must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met (relevance to review objective): the study does not examine drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply (whole-brain task maps are reported). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI reinforcement-learning investigation of reward vs loss (monetary) prediction error in schizophrenia, with whole-brain group-level PE-related activation maps reported. While it provides whole-brain task-evoked results (satisfying I6) and reports results in figures/tables (I7), it does not involve the types of decision-making tasks specified by the inclusion criteria (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). The task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning gain/loss task rather than contrasts such as “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or perceptual difficulty contrasts, so it fails I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The article is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward–related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Although the study is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI investigation of perceptual decision making (faces vs houses) and meets the listed neuroimaging task criteria, its stimuli and task probe perceptual/category decisions rather than reward-cue reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making: low vs high sensory evidence), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported in figures/tables/text). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore excluded for not addressing the review objective (reward cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete.

The study performed task-based fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning task (decision-making under uncertainty), modeling contrasts that index choice under high uncertainty (shift>stay) and outcome processing (reward>punishment). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TFCE-corrected across the whole brain) and provides coordinates/figures for significant clusters. Thus: I4 (fMRI during ambiguous/uncertain decision-making) is satisfied; I5 (within-task contrasts related to ambiguous/risky decision-making—shift>stay reflects choice under uncertainty) is satisfied; I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps) is satisfied; I7 (results reported as coordinates/figures/text) is satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study does not meet the review's decision-making task requirements. Inclusion: I6 and I7 are satisfied — the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps and describes whole-brain results in text/figures. Excluded because it does NOT meet I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined) and does NOT meet I5 (no within-task/between-task contrasts clearly corresponding to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making; the DDT contrast is Want>control for delay discounting which is intertemporal choice, not one of the required task types/examples). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED.

Although this study used fMRI during risky and ambiguous decision-making (wheel-of-fortune monetary gambles) and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts (e.g., Risk Gamble > Ambiguity Gamble; Gain > No Gain) with appropriate voxelwise/FWE correction, it does not address the stated meta-analysis objective: drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. The current study used monetary reward decisions and feedback rather than visual drug/natural reward cues. Therefore, despite meeting the listed decision-making inclusion criteria, it fails to address the review’s cue-reactivity objective and is not eligible for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by this paper.

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). Although it meets several technical inclusion criteria for fMRI decision-making studies — I4: yes (group fMRI while participants performed a risky lottery decision-making task); I5: yes (within-task parametric contrasts related to risk, e.g., ΔMin, ΔEV, and ΔU; PPI analyses and task-related modulatory contrasts are reported); I6: yes (group-level, whole-brain analyses are reported and whole-brain activations are summarized in tables); I7: yes (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). However, it fails the review’s topical requirement: it does not investigate cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual cues, but instead examines cognitive/affective processes in risky decision making for self vs others. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are met. Therefore excluded because the study does not address the review objective (cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it acquired fMRI while human adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains), and reports an explicit within-task contrast of interest (risky > safe) as well as a reward > punishment contrast. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (one-sample t-tests and between-group ANOVAs) with results described in tables and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, or non-empirical) were violated. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis focused on task-evoked whole-brain decision-making contrasts.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (high-risk vs low-risk gambles) and thus addresses risky decision-making (I4). The authors report within-task model-based contrasts related to risky choices (difference between high- and low-risk option weights and prediction-error regressors equivalent to risk-related contrasts) and behavioral contrasts (I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs with reported statistical maps, thresholding, and activation tables/figures (I6,I7). The full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (mixed gambles) with manipulations of expected value, uncertainty, and urgency. It reports within-task contrasts related to risk/EV (e.g., positive EV > negative EV, neutral vs. negative/positive) and interactions with urgency. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are described (SPM8; voxel-level p<0.001 with cluster-level correction) and whole-brain results are reported. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the HiLo task, a perceptual/ambiguous decision-making paradigm (uncertainty manipulation). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to ambiguity/uncertainty (linear uncertainty contrasts, 50% vs 100% comparisons, and incorrect > correct feedback). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted using FLAME with Gaussian random field cluster correction and significant clusters are reported; results are described in the text and figures. Thus it meets all required criteria for inclusion (I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

The study does not meet the key task-related inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. While it reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses (I6) and clearly describes whole-brain results/figures (I7), the experimental paradigm is a reinforcement-learning/probabilistic gain-loss learning task (reward vs. punishment prediction error encoding), not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) and I5 (a within-task or between-task contrast directly related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty, e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because required inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met.

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not address the meta-analysis objective (fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli). Although this is an fMRI perceptual decision-making study with appropriate within-task contrasts related to perceptual uncertainty and it reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (meets I4, I5, I6, I7), it does not investigate cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards or visual reward cues. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study involved human participants performing a risky decision-making task (a virtual sexual ‘hook up’ game) and reports task contrasts (SRD > implicit baseline; SRD > conversational) and between-group contrasts (Risky > Safe), satisfying inclusion criteria I4 and I5. However, the neuroimaging analyses were conducted and reported within predefined anatomical/functional ROIs (TFCE contrasts within four decision-making ROIs and ROI-based follow-ups). Although some covariate analyses were run at the whole-brain level with null results, the primary reported task-evoked group contrasts and cluster results are ROI-restricted and not presented as unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Therefore the study does not meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map). This places it within exclusion criterion E3 (reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain task map). I7 is not applicable because the required whole-brain task maps are not reported. Full text appears complete.

The study is a model-driven fMRI investigation of perceptual decision-making (GO/NO-GO) examining predictive information and decision thresholds. While it meets methodological inclusion criteria (I4: a perceptual decision-making fMRI task; I5: within-task parametric contrasts related to decision-making; I6: group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses; I7: results and coordinates reported), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. There is no manipulation or contrast involving reward cue exposure or cue-reactivity. Therefore it does not address the review topic and must be excluded. Exclusion IDs met: none of E3–E6 apply. Included criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Included criteria not met (regarding review objective): study does not involve reward-related cue-reactivity or drug/natural reward visual cues.

Although this manuscript reports an fMRI Wheel-of-Fortune risky decision-making task with within-task contrasts (magnitude, probability, risk) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meeting I4, I5, I6, I7), it does not address the stated meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. The paradigm involves monetary choice and outcome feedback rather than presentation of visual drug/natural reward cues; therefore it fails to meet the topical requirement of the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are otherwise triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although the full text reports a group-level, whole-brain fMRI study of decision-making under uncertainty (Shannon entropy) and provides task contrasts and PPI connectivity, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli. The task involved monetary choice between delayed/probabilistic rewards (economic decisions), not presentation of drug or natural reward cues or visual cue-reactivity contrasts. Therefore the study is not relevant to the review topic and is excluded on that basis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making (card-guessing/betting) task, with within-task contrasts examining risk-related effects (main effects of control, previous outcome, and previous control × previous outcome during betting and feedback). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates (tables and figures), satisfying the requirement that whole-brain task-evoked results be provided (coordinates/tables). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met.

Although this paper meets the technical fMRI decision-making inclusion criteria (see below), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective. The review seeks fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (cue-reactivity). This study examines adolescent risk processing during an economic lottery decision-making task (monetary gambles) and cognitive control (MSIT), not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward cues. Therefore it is not conceptually eligible for a meta-analysis of reward cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task - lottery choice), I5 (within-task contrast related to risk: high vs low CV), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analysis reported), I7 (results/coordinates reported in text/appendices). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED because it does not address reward cue-reactivity using visual drug/natural reward cues required by the meta-analysis objective.

This study measured BOLD responses to parametrically varied motion stimuli during passive viewing while subjects performed an independent fixation luminance task. It reports analyses averaged over retinotopically-defined visual areas and fits population response functions; it does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. It also does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task contrast of the type required (participants performed an independent fixation discrimination task unrelated to the motion stimulus; no perceptual decision contrasts such as hard>easy or low coherence>high coherence tied to an explicit task were reported). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only / no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task related to the stimulus), I5 (no within- or between-task decision-making contrasts), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not address the review objective of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses reported) and I7 (whole-brain results described in text/supplement). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (the in-scanner task is a monetary card-guessing reward expectancy paradigm rather than a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task focused on drug/natural reward cues) and I5 (no within-task contrast explicitly framed as risky>safe or analogous risk/ambiguity contrast using drug/natural reward cues). Because the primary meta-analysis objective requires studies of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, this monetary reward task does not meet the review objective despite having whole-brain results. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study in human adults using a perceptual decision-making task (backward-masking majority function), meeting I4. It includes within-task contrasts tied to perceptual difficulty/information rate (main effects of information entropy, reciprocal of exposure time, and their interaction; effectively hard>easy-like contrasts), meeting I5. All analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain GLM/regression results with tables/figures and cluster-corrected thresholds, satisfying I6 and I7. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete = true). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps, empirical data reported).

This study does not address the review objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). The task involves probabilistic inference about animal 'sectors' (latent causes), not cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards. It also does not contain the required within-task contrasts related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., 'risky > safe', 'ambiguous > non-ambiguous', 'hard > easy'); the main analyses are representational similarity analyses (multivariate pattern similarity) rather than condition-based task contrasts. Although the paper reports whole-brain searchlight RSA results, it lacks conventional group-level, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts of the sort required by the inclusion criteria. Therefore it fails to meet the inclusion criteria and is not relevant to the meta-analysis.

Although this is an event-related fMRI group study with whole-brain analyses (I6) and reports coordinates/figures (I7), it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. The task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm probing reversal learning and negative feedback processing, and the reported contrasts (e.g., final reversal errors vs correct responses, probabilistic errors vs correct) are not contrasts of risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty as required by I4–I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that conducted risky decision-making (probability discounting) and intertemporal decision-making during scanning. It reports within-task parametric contrasts relating neural activity to subjective value for probabilistic (risky) decisions and compares PD to DD. Analyses are group-level whole-brain GLMs (random-effects second-level SPM), with voxelwise results reported as coordinates and figures (supplemental tables referenced), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk via subjective-value regressors and PD>DD comparisons), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I7 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is referenced but not required to establish whole-brain results. Hence include.

Although this is an empirical human fMRI study of decision-making with group-level whole-brain task maps and within-task contrasts, it does not address the stated meta-analysis objective: drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The experiment involves a monetary limited-offer sequential decision task (risky choice/planning) rather than cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual cues. Therefore, despite satisfying the fMRI/task-related inclusion criteria, it is not relevant to the review topic and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a probabilistic monetary decision-making task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts and correlation analyses tied to risk-related variables (expected value, uncertainty/variance, temporal-difference prediction error, reward outcome), and investigates contrasts across EV/RM/TD error conditions. Analyses were performed at the group level using SPM2 with whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise statistics (with whole-brain correction and SVCs) and results are reported as coordinates, figures, and corrected group-level maps. Thus it satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans who performed a probabilistic instrumental (decision-making) task with visual cues and monetary outcomes. The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts related to decision variables (left/right option values, state value, prediction errors) and contrasts of left vs right responses. Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM random-effects analyses with statistical maps and voxel coordinates reported. These meet the review’s inclusion criteria for a risky/decision-making fMRI task (I4), at least one within-task contrast related to decision-making (I5), whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps (I6), and acceptable reporting of results in maps/coordinates (I7). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although the study includes an fMRI probabilistic decision-making task with appropriate task vs control and last-trial contrasts and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, it does NOT address the review objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli). The task examines probabilistic/ambiguous decision-making (beads/fish tasks) in ARMS patients versus controls rather than cue-elicited reward reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Therefore it is not eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of reward cue-reactivity. Whole text appears complete.

The full text is a complete empirical fMRI study of probabilistic reversal learning (cognitive flexibility) with whole-brain group analyses and reported coordinates. It does NOT meet the review’s decision-making task requirements: (1) I4 not met — the task is a probabilistic reversal learning task focused on reward prediction errors/cognitive flexibility, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the inclusion examples; (2) I5 not met — no within-task or between-task contrasts explicitly related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) are reported — the main contrasts are parametric RPE effects and group comparisons of RPE processing. It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task effects reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making (random-dot motion) task with explicit reward cues (visual/auditory precues and colored background indicating monetary reward). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing rewarded vs nonrewarded trials during anticipatory and decision periods (R75/25 vs NR75/25; res-R75 vs res-NR75), which are directly relevant to perceptual decision-making and reward-cue reactivity. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM/random-effects contrasts with reported t-maps and coordinate tables (thresholding and cluster criteria described), meeting requirements for whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study does not involve functional MRI. Exclusion IDs met: none of the explicit exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply (so exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Inclusion IDs met: none (inclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (no fMRI scan during task), I5 (no within-task or between-task fMRI contrasts reported), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I7 (not applicable since no whole-brain results reported). Full text is complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is not eligible for the fMRI-based meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This study reports simultaneous EEG/fMRI during decision-making tasks that include probabilistic uncertainty and intertemporal (delay) choices (i.e., risky/ambiguous decision-making). Task-related fMRI contrasts were computed (each task vs control) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are presented and described (figures and statistical thresholds reported). The report therefore meets I4 (task-based risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast: task > control), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results presented in figures/tables and described in text). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Note: sample size is small (n=6), but that does not violate provided inclusion/exclusion rules.

The study uses an event-related fMRI Risky-Gains task and reports risky>safe contrasts, satisfying inclusion criteria I4 and I5. However, the reported results are presented as ROI analyses (percent signal change in pre-defined ROIs, ROI statistics) and there is no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or whole-brain coordinate table described as the primary task-evoked result. Therefore it does not meet I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion E3 (reports only ROI analyses without whole-brain results). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion rationale: Although this is an empirical fMRI study with a risky decision-making task, whole-brain group analyses, and reported contrasts, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of E3–E6 apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast: stock vs. bond, risky>safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (results/tables/contrast files provided in supplements). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: While I4–I7 are satisfied, the study does not examine visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards and therefore is not relevant to the review objective. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDE due to lack of topical relevance to the review question (not a cue-reactivity visual-stimuli study).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based risky decision-making fMRI. It acquired task-based fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART) (I4). The authors modeled risk-level (Pumps) and produced within-task, risk-related contrasts/parametric maps (risk level-related activation) (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were reported (one-sample t-test with cluster-level FWE correction; risk-level z-statistic maps) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6) and results are described in the text/figures/tables (I7). The paper also contains full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (E3), not solely resting-state/seed connectivity (E4) — although resting-state analyses are included, they do not replace the task activation maps — and it is an empirical fMRI study with within-task effects (not E5 or E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human males performing a risky decision-making task (BART) during MRI (I4). It includes within-task contrasts comparing risk versus control (parametric modulation: experimental green balloon > control orange balloon; decision contrasts cash > inflate) (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are conducted and reported with FWE correction and cluster coordinates (I6), with results presented in text, tables and figures (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), it is task activation (not only connectivity or resting-state), and includes whole-brain task effects alongside group interactions. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article meets all specified inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and should be INCLUDED.

This study should be excluded. It does involve fMRI during a probabilistic/ambiguous decision-making task (meets I4) and reports within-task comparisons between task stages (meets I5). However, it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain voxelwise results: analyses are ROI-based and multivariate within predefined ROIs, and the main reported results are ROI/multivariate statistics and selected-voxel maps rather than unmasked whole-brain activation maps. Therefore I6 (whole-brain evidence) is not met and Exclusion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

Although this study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses of a risky decision-making task with appropriate within-task parametric contrasts and voxelwise maps, it does not address the meta-analysis topic (drug or natural reward cue-reactivity to visual stimuli). Stimuli and paradigm involve monetary mixed-gambles rather than drug/natural reward cues, so it is not conceptually eligible for the review despite meeting methodological inclusion criteria.

Although this study meets the decision-making fMRI inclusion criteria (it is an fMRI study with a risky decision-making lottery task, reports within-task contrasts including parametric EV modulation and gain/loss contrasts, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results/tables), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. The task used explicit numerical lottery stimuli and choice/feedback evaluation rather than visual reward-cue exposure (drug or natural reward cues). Therefore it fails to meet the review’s primary objective and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study using the BART, a risky decision-making task. It meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task and between-task risk-related contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I7 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures). However, the study does not address the meta-analysis objective: drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (it examines monetary risk-taking, not cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not match the review objective despite meeting I4–I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study used task-based fMRI in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (risky decision-making). It reports within-task risk-related contrasts (parametric risk regressors) for active-choice and passive-no-choice conditions, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses with cluster correction and reports coordinates/figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not a non-empirical paper). Therefore it satisfies the required inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making whole-brain task activation and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Stoplight driving game) in the scanner, with explicit within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe decisions (Go > Stop) and outcome contrasts (Pass > Crash). Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 models with voxelwise FWE correction and reported peak coordinates/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus it meets I4 (task-based risky decision-making fMRI), I5 (risky>safe contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported as tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a methods/protocol fMRI experiment of risky and ambiguous decision-making and reports single-subject and representative neural results, but it does not provide clear group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps required for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-making) and I5 (task-related contrasts/regressors for risk and ambiguity). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear report of group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or coordinates in the full text provided). The study also does not address the stated meta-analysis objective of reward-related cue-reactivity to drug/natural cues. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude.

While the study is an empirical, whole-brain task fMRI investigation of risky decision making and meets the listed imaging inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. The task uses probabilistic deck choices with numeric stimuli and models risk prediction, not visual cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore, despite satisfying I4–I7, the study is not relevant to the review objective and is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (BART) and examines loss-aversion versus reward-seeking and infrequency effects. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risky decision-making: parametric contrasts like ChooseInflate*P(explode) and ChooseWin*P(explode)), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: the study does NOT address the review’s topical requirement of visual drug or natural reward cue-reactivity. Therefore it is not relevant to the meta-analysis despite meeting the methodological inclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human males performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task) with within-task contrasts (risky > safe; decision-making > control; wins > losses). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects) are reported with tables of coordinates and figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of tactile texture processing in adults with ASD, not a decision-making cue-reactivity study. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (no risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task was performed during scanning; participants received passive tactile stimulation) and I5 (no contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making such as “risky>safe” or “hard>easy”; contrasts are texture>rest and between-group texture differences). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in human participants using the risky-gains task (a risky decision-making paradigm). The authors report a within-task contrast of interest (risky > safe) and conduct group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 t-maps) with reported thresholds, clusters, figures and tables. ROI analyses are also present but whole-brain results are reported, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only effects, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling appraisal. Therefore the study satisfies I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked whole-brain risky decision-making contrasts.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART) during scanning, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risk decisions (pumping) following negative versus positive feedback (risk after negative > after positive), satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM contrasts with cluster-level FWE correction and results reported in whole-brain tables/figures and NeuroVault, satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition/analysis), Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human smokers performing a probabilistic (risky) decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) with visual stimuli and monetary rewards. It includes within-task contrasts (money > control; decision trials > control) that qualify as an experimental task > control contrast for risky-DM (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster correction and MNI coordinates (I6,I7). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Although risky>safe contrasts were not analyzed due to unequal trial counts, the money>control decision contrast meets the stated inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using an event-related gambling/guessing task with uncertain outcomes (risk/ambiguity) during the anticipation phase, satisfying the review objective. Evidence: (1) Task: an event-related gambling paradigm with uncertain outcomes (participants guess card color) assesses anticipation of reward/uncertainty, meeting I4. (2) Contrasts: within-task contrasts comparing anticipation of reward vs no-change (e.g., Ant $4 – No-ch $4), and grouping of win/lose vs no-change, directly indexing risk/uncertainty, meeting I5. (3) Analysis: voxel-wise, second-level group whole-brain analyses reported (p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster threshold), meeting I6. (4) Results are reported in text, tables, and figures (cluster coordinates and parameter estimates), meeting I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of perceptual two-choice decision-making (numerical and verbal tasks) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (numerical task > baseline; verbal task > baseline), a full-factorial group ANOVA, and multiple regression correlating diffusion-model parameters with whole-brain percent signal change, with results reported as thresholded statistical maps and peak coordinates. The full text provides methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses and contrasts. Therefore it satisfies the perceptual decision-making fMRI inclusion criteria and contains whole-brain task-evoked maps suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The full text is complete and reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked fMRI analyses (meets I6 and I7). However, the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm and the reported contrasts (final reversal errors vs nonswitch errors; nonswitch errors vs correct responses) index cognitive flexibility and feedback processing rather than the review’s target domains of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. The study does not report contrasts of the form required by I5 (e.g., risky > safe, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, hard > easy), nor does it clearly operationalize the task as risky or ambiguity decision-making per the inclusion list (I4/I5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5 while meeting I6 and I7.

This study collected fMRI while human subjects performed a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion reports), so it satisfies I4. However, it does not report a within-task or between-task voxelwise contrast related to perceptual difficulty (e.g., “hard>easy”, “low coherence>high coherence”) or similar (I5 not met), and it does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; analyses are ROI-based multivariate reconstructions rather than unmasked whole-brain task maps (I6 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI/multivariate ROI analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical human fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (ring-size discrimination) and includes within-task stimulus contrasts (S vs L, M, and choice-related contrasts), the analyses are restricted to primary visual cortex (V1) and population/ROI-based voxel selection. The paper does not report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps required by the review. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) while satisfying inclusion criteria I4 and I5 but failing I6. Full text appears complete.

Although this study uses fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (coherent motion) and reports condition-wise and group analyses, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria I4–I7 are satisfied (fMRI perceptual decision task; within-task contrasts across coherence/difficulty levels; group-level whole-brain analyses reported; results described in text/figures). However, the primary research question and task are about autism and visual motion perception, not reward-related cue-reactivity; therefore the study is not relevant to the review objective and is excluded. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Cannot verify key inclusion criteria: I4 (unclear whether task qualifies as risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making—while the abstract mentions predictability/uncertainty, task details are lacking), I5 (no information on task-related contrasts such as ambiguous>non-ambiguous or risk>certainty), I6/I7 (no access to methods/results to confirm group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps or coordinate tables). The study also appears to focus on reward-related trial-and-error learning rather than visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards, so it may not address the meta-analysis objective. Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E6 can be confirmed from the available text. Inclusion criteria met: none can be confirmed. Inclusion criteria not met/not verifiable: I4, I5, I6, I7. Request full article (methods/results) for re-screening.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human adolescents performing the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making), with task-related analyses that model activation as a function of balloon size (a within-task parametric risk regressor). Group-level, voxelwise t-tests were performed and whole-brain statistical maps and peak coordinates are reported (with multiple-comparison correction via Bonferroni/FWE and Monte Carlo simulations).
