Thus the paper meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task risk-related effect via parametric correlation), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without unmasked task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study had human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (odd/even with PASS option) during fMRI (meets I4). The paper reports the within-task contrast uncertain>certain and between-group comparisons (meets I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with reported thresholding and cluster tables/figures (meets I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, and include unmasked whole-brain task effects (E3–E5 not met). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports an fMRI investigation in human participants (young smokers and nonsmokers) performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task) during scanning. It includes within-task contrasts related to risk (e.g., PumpsParametric > ControlParametric, PumpsAvg > ControlAvg), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL, cluster-corrected; tables of significant clusters and MNI coordinates are provided), and reports results in text/tables/figures. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual cues. While it reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (I6) and presents whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I7), it does not involve a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as required (I4) nor does it include the required within-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (I5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual detection task (visual signals at threshold), i.e., a perceptual decision-making paradigm. The authors report within-task, task-evoked contrasts comparing response outcomes (misses vs. hits, misses vs. correct rejections) and interactions with TMS, which are relevant perceptual decision-making contrasts. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, and results are reported with coordinates and family-wise error cluster correction (group-level random effects), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 and is eligible for inclusion.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a sequential value-based buying/rejecting task with probabilistic information, which constitutes risky/ambiguous decision-making. The paper includes within-task contrasts and parametric modulators related to ambiguity/evidence accumulation (e.g., accumulated value P(good|e)t, accumulated evidence |LE(buy)t|, unambiguous vs ambiguous trials), and tests trial-by-trial contrasts. Analyses were performed at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise statistics (FWE-corrected results reported and peak coordinates/tables provided). Thus it satisfies I4 (human fMRI during decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to ambiguous/risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is an empirical human fMRI study using a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with parametric difficulty (suprathreshold vs perithreshold) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported, it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Therefore it is outside the review’s topical scope and must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast related to perceptual difficulty: suprathreshold > perithreshold), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported in figures/tables/supplement). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that explicitly manipulated ambiguity in a decision-making task (ambiguous vs. generalization contexts) and used trial-wise model-based contrasts (Shannon entropy of prior belief) tied to ambiguity. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses with cluster-level FWE-corrected activations (including hippocampus, amygdala, fusiform, precuneus) and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described and illustrated. Thus it meets I4 (human fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (ambiguity-related within-task parametric contrast), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported), and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is a human fMRI study with an ambiguous decision-making task and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts (Uncertain > Certain) and seed-based connectivity, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward-related visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast ambiguous > certain), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: the study does not examine cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards (does not present drug/natural reward visual cues), therefore it fails to address the review objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Blackjack), with explicit within-task contrasts comparing high-risk versus low-risk and suboptimal versus optimal decisions (e.g., high-risk hits > low-risk hits; low-risk sits > high-risk sits). Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed and whole-brain results are reported (Talairach coordinates and tables/figures for activations), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7.

Full text appears complete. This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making across development that includes human participants performing a risky decision task (meets I4), reports within-task contrasts/parametric effects related to risk and advice (meets I5), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps (meets I6) reported in text/tables/supplement (meets I7). However, it does not address the review objective of cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual stimuli (i.e., it examines decision-making and advice effects, not visual cue-reactivity to substances or natural rewards). This study reports simultaneous EEG/fMRI during a perceptual categorization task (Mooney images), satisfying I4. The fMRI analysis includes within-task contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (object vs. scrambled/inverted conditions, HF>LF and LF>HF contrasts), satisfying I5. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM results are reported with cluster-correction and peak coordinates (Table 1 and statistical maps), satisfying I6 and I7. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical fMRI in healthy adults). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and is included.

This is an empirical human fMRI study (1.5T) in adults performing a risky economic decision-making task (mixed 50/50 monetary gambles). The paper reports within-task contrasts (gain > loss and a neural loss aversion [NLA] contrast) and group-level, whole-brain SPM8 analyses with coordinates and tables (uncorrected p<0.001), and ROI correlations. Thus it meets I4 (task-based fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk/loss), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I7 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes whole-brain task effects, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

Although this is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (model-free prediction errors and model-based minus model-free prediction error contrasts), it does not examine risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as required. The task is a sequential model-based/model-free reinforcement-learning paradigm focused on reward prediction errors and the balance of control, not contrasts such as ‘risky > safe’, ‘ambiguity > non-ambiguous’, or perceptual difficulty contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (at least one within-task or between-task contrast mapped to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) are not met. Inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are met (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps reported and acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study does not address the review objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and does not implement a decision-making task as required by I4. Although it contains a between-group comparison of ambiguous versus differential outcome groups and reports whole-brain group-level analyses/coordinates, the paradigm is instruction-based outcome-integration (learning S–R–O associations) rather than a risky/ambiguous perceptual decision-making task probing cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (between-group contrast ambiguous vs differential outcomes), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses performed), I7 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required by the review objective). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply, but failure to meet I4 requires exclusion.

The study uses a probabilistic reversal learning task to probe reward prediction errors in alcohol-dependent patients and controls, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Therefore it fails I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and I5 (task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). The full text includes group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses and reported coordinates, so I6 and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key task-related inclusion criteria (I4, I5) are not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (N=30) that used a sequential investment task involving risky decision making. fMRI data were acquired during task performance and within-task regressors (risk-sensitive TD errors and Q-values) were used as parametric modulators; these produced significant whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain cluster-corrected p<.05; coordinates and cluster sizes reported). Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/modulators related to risky decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), and I7 (coordinates and figures/tables provided). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, fMRI preprocessing/analysis, and coordinates provided).

This is an fMRI study of statistical learning and prediction using structured vs random symbol sequences. While it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (meets I6) and presents whole-brain results in text/figures (meets I7), it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (participants performed prediction/statistical-learning tasks, not risky/uncertain choice or perceptual difficulty contrasts). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map required for this meta-analysis and reports analyses limited to ROI-based decoding (E3). It does include fMRI during a perceptual task (2IFC orientation detection and in-scanner decoder runs), satisfying I4. However, it does not report the required within-task/between-task whole-brain contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (I5 not met) nor provide whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I6 not met). Therefore it fails to meet all inclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a two-choice prediction decision-making task with varying error-rate conditions (20%, 50%, 80%), satisfying the requirement of an fMRI scan during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task. The authors report within-task contrasts (e.g., 20% vs 80% error-rate) examining error-rate-dependent activation, meeting the contrast requirement. Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps using AFNI with cluster correction and report cluster coordinates/tables (Table 3 and figures), fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that explicitly manipulated ambiguity in decision-making (internal subjective, external subjective, and external veridical color-matching conditions). It includes within-task contrasts relevant to ambiguous decision-making (ESD vs EVD, ISD vs EVD, ISD vs ESD) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with figures and tables of voxel coordinates. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion sections. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is included.

This fMRI study examines social decision-making in the Ultimatum Game (unfair vs fair offers; decision to accept/reject) in healthy women. While it reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (satisfying I6) and presents results in tables/figures (I7), it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as required (I4 not met) and does not include within-task contrasts matching the risk/ambiguity/perceptual examples (I5 not met). Additionally, the study does not address drug or natural reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli (outside the review objective). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply and the full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (visual object categorization: tools vs musical instruments) while ignoring concurrent sounds, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., incongruent > congruent, degraded vs intact visual reliability, interactions with reaction time), meeting I5. Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain SPM random-effects analyses with reported cluster- and voxel-wise results and coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying I6 and I7. The full text includes methods, whole-brain results, tables of coordinates, and discussion; not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical fMRI in healthy adults, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain reporting and is INCLUDED.

This study is an fMRI investigation of risky decision-making (Balloon Analogue Risk Task) in substance-dependent individuals, using monetary rewards and parametric modulators of explosion probability. While the full text is complete and the study meets the technical inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4: an fMRI scan during a risky decision-making task; I5: within-task contrasts/modulators related to risk levels; I6: group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported; I7: whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective (drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) because it does not present or analyze visual drug/natural reward cue-reactivity. Therefore it is not relevant to the stated review objective and should be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met (relevant to review objective): study does not examine visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. Exclusion criteria applied: none ([]) .

The study is an fMRI investigation of truth-telling and risk propensity using a social Communication Game, not a drug or natural reward cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli. Although it collected whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (I6) and reports results in text/tables/figures (I7), and involved an fMRI decision-making task under asymmetric information (I4), it does not include a within-task contrast of the type required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (I5) nor any cue-reactivity contrasts (e.g., drug cue > neutral cue). Therefore it does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded.

The full text is complete. This study used whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses and reports voxelwise task-evoked results (satisfies I6 and I7). However, it does not meet the critical task-related inclusion criteria: the fMRI session involved probabilistic reward-learning/confirmation and analysis of reward prediction error and emotional modulation (fearful vs neutral faces), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined in I4. Accordingly, no within-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, “hard > easy”) are reported (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because I4 and I5 are not satisfied.

The full text reports event-related fMRI in healthy human participants performing a visual classification task with deterministic, probabilistic (ambiguous), and random conditions. It contains within-task contrasts directly comparing probabilistic versus deterministic classification (Prob-CP > Det-CP), which maps onto ambiguous > non-ambiguous decision-making contrasts (I4,I5). The paper includes group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with reported activation clusters/tables and exploratory whole-brain results (meets I6 and I7). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used a perceptual decision-making task (2AFC orientation discrimination) and reports ROI-based MVPA and regression analyses within retinotopically defined visual areas (V1–V3). However, it does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or standard whole-brain contrasts (the main results are ROI/MVPA-based and single-trial classifier/regression outputs). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation reporting and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results without whole-brain maps). Inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task) is satisfied. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported within-task/between-task whole-brain contrasts of the type required for meta-analysis) and I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level task maps and coordinate reporting (meets I6 and I7). However, the task is a value-based Becker–DeGroot–Marschak willingness-to-pay decision task (food vs nonfood), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as required. The reported contrasts are reward-category and sleep-state interactions (e.g., food>nonfood, valuation signals), not risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED because the experimental task and contrasts do not match the meta-analysis’ required decision-making domains (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic category learning task (PCLT) and contrasts PCLT > control (PMCT), but it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (e.g., risky > safe, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, hard > easy). Although the paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps (meeting I6) and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures (meeting I7), it does not satisfy I4 (task type) or I5 (task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Although this fMRI study meets the formal task-related inclusion criteria (see below), it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug- or natural reward–related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. It is a decision-making (modified Iowa Gambling Task) study examining risky decision-making and group differences in prefrontal activation in substance users versus controls, not a visual cue-reactivity paradigm presenting drug or natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast including risky > safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6. Inclusion criteria not met for the meta-analysis objective: the study does not probe visual drug/natural reward cue-reactivity (task is decision-making with monetary/gambling outcomes rather than visual drug/natural reward cues). Full text is complete.

The full text reports an fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) performed during scanning (meets I4). Task-related contrast (decision > fixation) was used to index decision-making and relates to risk-related task activity (meets I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain mediation mapping (MEPM) and presents whole-brain results in text/figures/tables, satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise analyses (meets I6 and I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes whole-brain task effects).

Full text reports an fMRI study using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making paradigm (satisfies I4). The authors report within-task parametrically modulated contrasts related to risk (inflation choices, successful inflation outcomes, explosion outcomes) and correlations with behavior/traits (satisfies I5). Second-level/group analyses are whole-brain/voxelwise with cluster- and voxel-level (FWE/FDR) corrections and peak coordinates reported (satisfies I6 and I7). The manuscript includes full methods, results, tables, and figures describing whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met.

This study does not address the review objective (reward-related cue-reactivity) and fails to meet required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI task is a prediction/statistical-learning task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty are reported), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrast maps appropriate for meta-analysis of cue-reactivity are provided). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are specifically met (the paper reports whole-brain ICA-derived component maps and network analyses but these are not the voxelwise task contrasts required). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study used an intertemporal (delay discounting) monetary decision-making task and reports a Hard > Easy contrast at the group level (whole-brain analysis). However, it does not employ a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required by I4 (this is an intertemporal delay-discounting task, not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded. Whole-brain group task results are reported (Hard > Easy), satisfying I5 and I6, and reporting is acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The full text describes an fMRI gambling paradigm (risky decision-making) performed by human participants and reports task-related contrasts that directly compare risk levels (e.g., high-risk > low-risk; group×risk interactions and post-hoc high- vs low-risk contrasts). Analyses were performed as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM models with reported cluster coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values (tables/figures provided). Reporting in tables/figures/text includes whole-brain results. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not address the meta-analysis topic of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It instead reports an fMRI study of risky decision-making (Iowa Gambling Task) with message framing in substance-dependent vs. non-dependent participants. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast defined as risky/bad deck > safe/good deck), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). However, the study fails the review’s topical requirement (not a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting drug/natural reward visual cues), so it is not eligible for this cue-reactivity meta-analysis. fulltext_incomplete=false

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult humans performing a binary trust task that constitutes a risky/social decision-making paradigm (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to risk/trust (e.g., trusting > not trusting; human counterpart > computer mediator) and subgroup contrasts (BA vs NBA) (meets I5). Analysis was conducted with SPM at the group (second)-level using whole-brain voxelwise inference, reporting peak coordinates and FWE-corrected effects (meets I6), and whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures (meets I7). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and fMRI preprocessing/model details; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This study used an fMRI probabilistic loss-learning (reinforcement learning) task and model-based prediction-error contrasts (δ+, δ-), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. Reported task contrasts focus on model-derived prediction errors and loss-avoidance rather than contrasts like “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”. Crucially, the imaging analyses were masked to the striatum (ROI mask) rather than reported as unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, indicating ROI-focused results. Therefore the manuscript fails to meet inclusion criteria I4, I5, and I6 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses/no whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps of reward prediction error signals (satisfying I6) and presents these in figures/functional masks (satisfying I7), it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks as defined by the review (it uses a probabilistic reversal learning/reward-learning paradigm) and does not report contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual-DM (e.g., “risky>safe”, “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”, or “hard>easy”). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

While this study includes group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses (random-effects, voxelwise maps reported with coordinates) and reports task contrasts (e.g., smiley>frowney, high>low predictive value), it does not meet the review’s scope and core inclusion requirements. Specifically, it does not investigate drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity paradigms (passive or active cue-reactivity to reward-associated stimuli) and is not primarily a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as required by I4. The contrasts reported probe feedback-related reward processing and predictive-value effects in an implicit classification learning task rather than standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., risk>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore I4 and I5 are not satisfied even though whole-brain reporting criteria (I6, I7) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study investigates hierarchical Bayesian learning and precision-weighted prediction errors during an audio-visual associative learning task, not drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. It does not employ a risky, ambiguous, or classic perceptual decision-making contrast (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence); instead analyses focus on parametric modulators of computational variables (ε2, ε3, choice PE). While the report includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps (fulfilling I6) and presents whole-brain results in the text/tables (I7), it does not meet I4 (task type) nor I5 (required decision-making contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the review objective and fails to meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5.

The study does not investigate drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and does not employ a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis objective. It uses a probabilistic reinforcement learning (stimulus/feedback) paradigm with Japanese character stimuli and contrasts related to learning (stimulus vs feedback; early vs late learning), not risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, voxel-wise task-evoked analyses reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no contrasts matching risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this fMRI study includes a perceptual decision-making numerosity comparison task and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts related to perceptual difficulty/congruity analogous to hard>easy), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study issues). Primary reason for exclusion: the study’s experimental focus is numerosity/non-numerical magnitude accumulation, not reward cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards; thus it does not address the review objective and is ineligible for inclusion.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the primary task-domain inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (the paper reports whole-brain, cross-subject offline whole-brain classification and reports discriminating volumes/voxel-wise weights) and I7 (whole-brain results are described in the text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is the social economic ultimatum game, which is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined) and I5 (no within-task contrast framed as risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as “risky>safe” or “high uncertainty>low uncertainty” is reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study does not examine drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual cues; it investigates category learning using a rule-plus-exception task. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is category-learning, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making), I5 (no within-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making), I6 (analyses are ROI-focused/high-resolution MTL and striatum with ROI-based group alignment rather than a whole-brain voxelwise task activation map), and I7 (not applicable because whole-brain results are not reported). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (reports ROI analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore EXCLUDED.

Although this study conducted whole-brain fMRI in human participants performing a visual perceptual decision-making (categorization) task and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Far > Flanking, parametric contrasts of distance from decision bound/prototype) using voxelwise SPM analyses, it does not investigate drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. The meta-analysis objective is specifically to synthesize fMRI studies of drug and natural reward cue-reactivity to visual stimuli; this paper is a category learning/generalization study using Gabor patches with no reward-cue, drug-cue, or natural-reward stimuli or contrasts related to cue-reactivity. Therefore, despite meeting inclusion criteria I4–I7 (perceptual decision task, relevant within-task contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise results reported, acceptable reporting), it does not address the review objective and should be excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic sequential decision-making task with monetary outcomes (i.e., risky/probabilistic decision-making). The authors report within-task, task-evoked contrasts/parametric modulators (state prediction error and reward prediction error) at decision and outcome stages. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (FWE-corrected results reported), with results presented in tables and figures. Thus the paper satisfies the required criteria for task type, contrasts, and whole-brain reporting.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I4: the fMRI scans were conducted during passive free-viewing of faces and an emotion regulation (reappraise vs maintain) task, not during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. It does include contrasts comparing ambiguous (surprised) versus neutral faces (Surprise>Neutral), satisfying I5, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (with cluster correction), satisfying I6 and acceptable reporting per I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because I4 is not met (fMRI task is not a decision-making paradigm), despite meeting I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study in healthy adult humans that manipulated reward probability/uncertainty using a slot-machine paradigm (risky/ambiguous decision context). It reports within-task contrasts directly related to risk/uncertainty (e.g., S1Slot_B > S1Slot_A; DelaySlot_B > DelaySlot_A and other risk/uncertainty contrasts). Analyses used group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise statistical mapping with coordinates and tables (thresholds and clusters reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, paradigm, fMRI acquisition, GLM), Results, Figures/Tables and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied.

(a) No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task parametric contrast of risk/CV), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (whole-brain results clearly described and peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study administered the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a risky decision-making task) to human participants during whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI and reports within-task contrasts (Choose Inflate vs. Choose Win; Outcome Inflate vs. Outcome Explode) including parametric modulation by explosion probability. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with cluster correction are reported and coordinates/tables/figures are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (framing task) during scanning, includes within-task contrasts operationalizing risk/framing (e.g., (Gsure + Lgamble) − (Ggamble + Lsure)), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables and figures of activations. Therefore it satisfies the decision-task requirement, contains relevant contrasts, and provides whole-brain task-evoked results (tables and ROI/SVC reported but accompanied by whole-brain maps). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates risky decision-making. I4: fMRI was conducted while participants performed risky decision tasks (accept/reject and selection gambling tasks). I5: The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric effects related to risk (variance correlates), choice (accept > reject), and valence (gain > loss). I6: Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported, with cluster-level FWE correction. I7: Whole-brain results are presented and tabulated (Tables 1 and 2) and described in the text. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task-evoked whole-brain maps, and is empirical. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps were performed and reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates/tables and figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm in PD, not clearly defined as a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task per the specified examples) and I5 (the reported contrasts are final reversal errors vs correct responses and related error-type contrasts, not contrasts explicitly indexing risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty such as “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I4 and I5 required for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts.

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). It collected fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (numerical/verbal two-choice RT), so I4 is satisfied. However, it does not report conventional group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., perceptual task > control) suitable for inclusion: analyses are ICA-based component spatial maps and component-task regressions rather than univariate GLM contrasts. Therefore the study fails I5/I6 and matches exclusion criterion E4 (ICA/task-connectivity only without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

The study investigates fMRI responses to visual food cues (fattening vs. non-fattening) during passive viewing and an ad libitum eating paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. It does not report within-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty (I4 and I5 not met). Although fMRI preprocessing and ROI analyses are described, the paper’s primary reported results are ROI-based activations and a nested case-control ROI analysis; no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps are reported for inclusion (I6 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria applied: none. Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing decision-making tasks (prisoner’s dilemma and stag hunt) during whole-brain scanning. It includes an explicit within-study contrast of task conditions (PD vs SH) that indexes differences in risky/mixed-motive/uncertain decision-making, reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (cluster-corrected) and provides results in tables/figures/text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets I4 (human fMRI during decision-making tasks), I5 (within/between-task contrast related to decision-making: PD–SH), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analysis), and I7 (results clearly reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of text-based recalibration of speech perception (auditory perceptual decision-making). While it meets methodological inclusion criteria I4 (perceptual decision-making task: /aba/ vs /ada/ categorization), I5 (task-related contrasts/post-test trials), I6 (group-level whole-brain RFX GLM maps corrected for multiple comparisons), and I7 (results reported as whole-brain maps/figures), it does NOT address the review’s topical objective: drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study investigates audiovisual language/reading effects, not reward cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Therefore excluded due to topic mismatch (does not address reward cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports ROI-based habenula analyses without any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a risky decision-making task) and I5 (within-task contrasts related to risk, e.g., loss vs. win; high vs. low loss probability). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map reported; functional acquisition was limited to 23 slices centered on the epithalamus) and I7 (no whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article must be excluded from this meta-analysis because it violates E3 and lacks required whole-brain task-evoked maps for inclusion.

This fMRI study used a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports contrasts such as high-risk > low-risk and high-risk > equal-risk, satisfying inclusion criteria I4 and I5. However, the article reports ROI-based analyses (small-volume correction within pre-specified prefrontal ROIs) and does not present an unmasked group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map in the main text; whole-brain results are not provided as coordinates or figures that reflect an unmasked task effect. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy adults performing the Salience Attribution Test, a task with probabilistic (uncertain) reward cues and speeded responses. The authors report within-task contrasts that compare high- vs low-probability reward cue features (adaptive reward prediction) and contrasts probing cues with identical (ambiguous/uncertain 50%) reward probabilities (aberrant reward prediction). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are performed and whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (FWE-corrected clusters and coordinates), with supplementary VOI/SVC analyses; results are described in detail in the text and coordinates are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies I4 (fMRI during a task involving uncertainty/ambiguous reward cues), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing high vs low probability / ambiguous cues), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I7 (coordinates and whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in humans (adolescent females) in which participants made risky decisions (likelihood to have sex) with explicit high-risk vs low-risk conditions. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts including high-risk > low-risk and a targeted contrast Boys (High-risk − Low-risk) vs. (Food (High-risk − Low-risk) + Item (High-risk − Low-risk)). Analyses were performed at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise statistics (voxel p<.001, cluster extent threshold) and significant clusters/tables/figures are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting and is eligible for inclusion.

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward cue-reactivity to visual stimuli); it instead reports a risky decision-making (BART) task and model-based effective connectivity (GIMME) results. Inclusion criteria: I4 is met (fMRI during a risky decision-making task). Inclusion criteria I5 (at least one within-task or between-task voxelwise contrast related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map as the target analysis) are not clearly satisfied in the manuscript: the primary analyses are effective/connectivity-based, and although the authors note univariate/main effects are available on NeuroVault, the paper does not present a clear group-level whole-brain task contrast (voxelwise) suitable as the target map for this meta-analysis. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

Although this paper reports an empirical, whole-brain group fMRI study of risky decision-making (Stop > Go and Go > Stop contrasts) and includes whole-brain voxelwise results and tables, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual stimuli. The task is a driving-simulation decision paradigm probing risk, not cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task risky>safe contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (results reported in tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6. Therefore excluded because it does not address the review objective (reward cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing an explicit risky decision-making task (Self trials where participants choose gamble vs sure $10), and includes within-task parametric contrasts for risk (trial-by-trial risk regressor) and expected value. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected cluster-level results and tables of coordinates), fulfilling whole-brain evidence reporting. Results (caudate, mPFC, dlPFC, etc.) are presented as whole-brain maps/tables. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; contains task activation maps; empirical data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, SI).

This study used fMRI during a monetary delay-discounting (intertemporal choice) task in remitted-anorexia nervosa and control women, but does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Specifically, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by I4 (intertemporal/delay discounting is a distinct domain), and it does not provide a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map required by I6. Analyses were performed within predefined ROIs with small-volume correction and reported ROI clusters/coordinates rather than an unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical map; therefore exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task domain not one of risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (no specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise map reported), I7 (not applicable because no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Hence exclude.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in humans performing a reinforcement-based decision-making task (Paper-Scissors-Rock) that manipulates uncertainty across early (learning/uncertain) vs late (familiar/predictable) trials. Relevant within-task contrasts (early vs late trials; group × decision-time interactions) are reported. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain linear mixed-effects analyses were conducted and thresholded; results and cluster coordinates are described (with supplementary tables), and a-priori region analyses are also reported. Thus the study provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for decision-making under uncertainty and meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary references).

The study is an fMRI experiment with whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (satisfies I6 and I7). However, it used a probabilistic reversal learning task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as specified (does not satisfy I4). The reported contrasts (e.g., negative vs positive feedback, reversal errors vs positive feedback, prediction-error-related regressors) do not correspond to the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (does not satisfy I5). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded because key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met.

Exclusion(s) met: E3 (study reports primarily ROI-focused analyses without reporting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Inclusion(s) met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/perceptual decision-making task — land vs. do-not-land trials), I5 (within-task contrasts modeled: decision trials vs. control; correct vs. incorrect). Inclusion(s) not met: I6 (no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation map or unmasked whole-brain task effect presented), I7 (no whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplementary materials). The full text is complete. Because the paper reports ROI-constrained analyses and does not present unmasked whole-brain task-evoked maps or coordinates required for inclusion, it must be excluded under E3.

This fMRI study does not investigate drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task analyses) and I7 (whole-brain results are clearly described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is social learning/trust and bandit tasks, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making as defined) and I5 (no contrasts related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making such as “risky>safe”, “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”, or “hard>easy”). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply based on the full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making paradigm (Wheel of Fortune), with an explicit within-task contrast of interest (high risk/reward > moderate risk/reward). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and corrected for multiple comparisons; whole-brain results are reported (figures/tables described). The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion—full text appears present. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a number-comparison selection task (a perceptual decision-making paradigm). It includes within-task contrasts (congruent vs switch control; incongruent vs non-switch control; switch vs non-switch) that index perceptual/decision difficulty and interference, satisfying I5. Scanning used group-level, mixed-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analysis with corrected thresholds, and results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps/peak coordinates and figures, meeting I6 and I7. The task is a perceptual decision-making task (magnitude comparisons), so I4 is met. No exclusion criteria apply: the study provides whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity), reports within-task contrasts (not only between-group), and is empirical. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the perceptual decision-making category of the meta-analysis.

Although the paper includes an fMRI experiment of human perceptual decision-making under ambiguity and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts of ambiguity (e.g., ambiguous > unambiguous) with voxelwise maps, it does not investigate drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (the meta-analysis objective). Therefore it does not address the review topic and should be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task ambiguity-related contrasts), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), I7 (results described in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: does not address reward cue-reactivity (topic of the meta-analysis). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports an fMRI experiment (Experiment 2) in which human participants performed a risky decision-making task (Stag hunt) during whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. The authors report a within-task contrast of interest (Stag > Rabbit) and conducted whole-brain two-sample t-tests in SPM8, with voxelwise results and cluster peak coordinates reported (and supplementary tables). The paradigm and reported analyses meet the specified inclusion criteria and do not violate listed exclusion criteria.

This manuscript reports fMRI in human participants (n=12 women) performing a sexual decision-making task that manipulated partner risk (high vs low) and asked likelihood-of-sex ratings. The authors report within-task contrasts comparing high vs low risk (e.g., low > high), present a random-effects whole-brain group SPM (voxel-wise p<.001 with cluster threshold) with Talairach coordinates and figures, and relate activation to behavior. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study satisfies I4 (risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task risky contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I7 (coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete.

This study does not address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward cue-reactivity to visual cues) and does not report the requisite decision-making contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps are reported) and I7 (whole-brain results are clearly described in the text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is a social/advice-based hierarchical learning task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review) and I5 (no within-task contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making, e.g., “risky > safe” or “ambiguous > non-ambiguous” — instead results focus on model-based prediction-error regressors). Exclusion criteria: none applicable (E3–E6 not met). Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that acquired task-based whole-brain BOLD data while participants made risky and perceptual decisions (choice to take a risky challenge and a subliminal vowel/consonant perceptual discrimination). The paper reports within-task contrasts at the group (random-effects) level, including choice-onset contrasts comparing Discouragement vs Control and successful-trial contrasts (Discouragement > Control), and presents voxelwise statistical maps/peak coordinates (with whole-brain cluster correction and SVC-described results). Thus it meets the requirements for (I4) scanned risky/perceptual decision-making, (I5) within-task contrasts related to decision-making, (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps, and (I7) reporting of whole-brain results with coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This study used fMRI to examine probabilistic reversal learning and prediction-error encoding in Huntington’s disease patients, not visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards. It reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps (and tables/figures) for prediction-error contrasts, so I6 (whole-brain evidence) and I7 (acceptable reporting in text/figures/tables) are satisfied. However, it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (it is a reinforcement/reversal learning task), and it does not report contrasts that map onto the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguity > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”), so I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an original, empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans using a choice reaction time (CRT) task that manipulates uncertainty/entropy across conditions (RA and RR). It constitutes a perceptual/decision-making task and reports within-task contrasts related to difficulty/uncertainty (linear contrasts of entropy/HA and HR across conditions). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM and single-trial analyses are performed and reported (thresholded statistical maps and supplementary tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full article is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the fMRI task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning/social face choice paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are NOT met. The study does meet I6 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses) and I7 (results clearly reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is an fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps reported (meets I6 and I7), it does NOT meet the critical design requirement I4: scanning was performed during a Pavlovian conditioning/imperative task in which participants passively viewed cues and pressed a location button, rather than performing a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Consequently the key inclusion contrast requirement I5 is not satisfied: the reported contrasts probe parametric stimulus-related signals (expected value, variance/uncertainty) during cue presentation rather than within-task or between-task decision contrasts such as “risky > safe” or “high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty” derived from participants making choices. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is ineligible for this meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult humans that manipulated perceptual uncertainty (three levels of prototype distortion) during a visual categorization task and analyzed neural responses. It reports within-task contrasts related to perceptual difficulty/uncertainty (parametric modulation of level of distortion; effectively ‘hard > easy’ effects) and training effects (untrained > trained). Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM second-level tests (results reported with tables of coordinates and whole-brain FDR-corrected maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Study is an fMRI investigation of perceptual decisions about faces (I4 satisfied) and reports group-level whole-brain statistical maps (e.g., switch>stay univariate maps) and figures (I6 and I7 satisfied). However, it does not report a within-task or between-task contrast specifically related to perceptual decision difficulty or perceptual-task versus control (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>control) as required by I5. The primary reported contrasts involve task switching (switch>stay) and decoding analyses rather than perceptual difficulty or explicit perceptual-task vs control contrasts; therefore I5 is not met and the study is excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis’ key task-based inclusion criteria. It uses the Monetary Incentive Delay task and a Probabilistic Selection Task to probe reward processing and reinforcement learning, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks (I4 not met). It does not report within-task contrasts related to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, “hard > easy”) (I5 not met). While fMRI was performed and exploratory whole-brain and PPI connectivity analyses are mentioned, the paper’s primary activation analyses are ROI-based and it does not provide a clear group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked activation map for the decision-making contrasts of interest (I6 not met). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports an fMRI investigation of implicit sequence learning and conflict-related cACC activity, not reward cue-reactivity or risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in tables/text). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (the fMRI task is an implicit serial reaction time/dual-task paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review), and I5 (no within-task contrasts relevant to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making, e.g., “risky>safe”, “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”, or “hard>easy”). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the article should be excluded from the meta-analysis because it fails to meet required task-related inclusion criteria (I4 and I5).

This is an fMRI study of probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) in schizophrenia that reports whole-brain task-evoked results. However, it does not address the meta-analysis objective of reward-related cue-reactivity to drug/natural rewards using visual stimuli, nor does it implement a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task with contrasts such as "risky > safe" or "ambiguity > non-ambiguous." It satisfies I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures), but fails I4 (task type) and I5 (required contrast types). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task involving choices between certain and risky monetary options, with happiness ratings sampled during the task. It includes task-related, within-task parametric contrasts (e.g., gamble/expected value and reward prediction error modulators tied to choice and outcome events) that relate to risky decision-making. Group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses were conducted (voxel-wise threshold P < 0.001) with reported peak coordinates and small-volume corrections; whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps were estimated and results reported via coordinates/figures. The full text (methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a human fMRI study that manipulated outcome uncertainty (ambiguity/risk) in a lottery task and tested neural responses. It includes within-task contrasts and parametric modulators related to outcome uncertainty (OU) and curiosity relief (e.g., increasing OU effects and Curiosity Relief–Yes > Curiosity Relief–No), reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster-level FWE correction, and provides tables of coordinates. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during ambiguous/risky task), I5 (task contrasts related to uncertainty/ambiguity), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I7 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. It uses an odor intensity evaluation under cognitive memory load (olfactory perception and cognitive load), not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task or contrasts (e.g., “risky>safe”, “ambiguity>non-ambiguous”, or “hard>easy”). The study does perform whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses and reports coordinates (so I6 and I7 are satisfied), but key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets I4 and I5: it is an fMRI study in human youth performing a decision-making reward task (number-guessing) and reports task contrasts (Win>Control, Loss>Control). However it does NOT meet I6 (whole-brain, unmasked voxelwise task-evoked maps). Analyses were conducted within an a priori reward-circuitry ROI/mask and significant clusters were determined within that mask; PPI connectivity was likewise constrained to the reward circuitry mask. Therefore exclusion criteria E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E5 (reports between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain task effect) are met. Because the review requires whole-brain group-level maps, this paper must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E3, E5.

The study employed an fMRI reinforcement-learning task (gain vs. loss-avoidance) and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses. However, it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as specified (I4 not met), nor does it report any contrasts of the type required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making (e.g., “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, “hard > easy”) (I5 not met). The paper does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps) and I7 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore, excluded because I4 and I5 are not satisfied.

This full-text reports whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI results from a probabilistic reversal-learning task (PRLT) and a Tower of London planning task in problem gamblers, smokers, and controls. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported using SPM2 with FDR correction) and I7 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the tasks are reversal-learning and planning, not framed as risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks per the meta-analysis definitions) and I5 (no contrasts that directly index risky vs safe, high- vs low-risk, ambiguity vs non-ambiguity, or hard vs easy perceptual decision-making; reported contrasts are monetary gain>baseline, loss>baseline, and reversal>baseline). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This study examines pseudo-resting-state functional connectivity and ‘brain age’ prediction during an emotional go/nogo task and relates predicted age to self-reported risk preference. It is NOT a drug or natural reward cue-reactivity study, and it does not employ a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for a risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrast; rather analyses focus on connectivity/PLSR prediction (pseudo-resting-state) without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria satisfied: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision-making), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map reported). Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analog Risk Task, a risky decision-making task (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts separating pump (risk) and cash-out (reward) events and examines risk- and reward-related activations (meets I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (whole-brain regressions with cluster correction) and results are reported with tables/coordinates and figures (meets I6 and I7). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: the study reports whole-brain task activations (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), includes task activation maps/coordinates, and is empirical. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for risky decision-making studies and is INCLUDED.

The full text is complete but the study does not address the review objective (fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual stimuli). It is an event-related fMRI study of risk perception for physical harm using textual scenarios. It does, however, meet the numbered inclusion criteria for the task/analysis: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts such as high-risk > low-risk and high-harm > low-harm), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction), and I7 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Primary exclusion rationale: domain mismatch with the meta-analysis objective (not a drug/natural reward cue-reactivity study using visual reward cues).

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not address the meta-analysis objective (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and does not meet the review’s task-specific inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported) and I7 (whole-brain results are reported as coordinates and described in text). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (the fMRI task is a social/moral financial decision task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review) and I5 (no within-task or between-task contrasts explicitly related to risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty, e.g., “risky>safe” or “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”). Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that employed a perceptual decision-making task (speeded 2-choice color discrimination) during whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. Relevant within-task contrasts are reported (e.g., task > no-task control, good-clock vs bad-clock, accessory vs no-accessory, and event-related stimulus/response analyses) that correspond to perceptual decision-making contrasts (perceptual task > control; manipulations of temporal uncertainty). Analyses were performed at the group level using whole-brain SPM2 and results are reported with thresholding and coordinate tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets I4–I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a Selection task involving choices between two simultaneously presented risky lotteries (risk defined as variance). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to risk and choice (e.g., choosing riskier > surer; contrasts for ∑Var, ΔVar, Var_chosen > Var_unchosen, chosen vs unchosen EV/SV), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with cluster-level FWE correction, and provides peak coordinates and tables. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task risk-related contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I7 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).
